The commercial emphasizes camaraderie and the ability to make the best of a challenging situation, culminating in a humorous resolution.

title: Hotel Hell with Griswolds
description: The Griswold family, from the "National Lampoon's Vacation" films, attempts a disastrous hotel stay, highlighting the chaos and inconvenience of traditional hotels.  The ad then contrasts this with the ease and comfort of a HomeAway vacation rental, showing the family happily relaxing in a spacious, well-equipped house. The humor lies in the exaggerated troubles of the hotel experience versus the calm of the alternative.  The commercial uses the comedic familiarity of the Griswolds to promote HomeAway as a superior vacation option.

title: Casket
description: A man is at a funeral, looking distraught.  He's about to lower the casket when he notices a bag of Doritos inside. He grabs them, discreetly eats a chip, and then his expression changes to one of pure joy. The humor is derived from the unexpectedness of finding comfort in Doritos during such a somber occasion. The final shot shows the casket descending into the ground.

title: Bridge is Out
description: The 2010 Budweiser Super Bowl ad, "Bridge is Out," depicts a Clydesdale horse and his foal traversing a flooded area, encountering various obstacles, such as a broken bridge.  The foal struggles initially but perseveres with the help of its father.  The ad emphasizes the strength and resilience of the Clydesdales, subtly mirroring the resilience of Budweiser.  It concludes with the Budweiser logo and a tagline. The ad features minimal human presence, focusing primarily on the horses.

title: Whale of a Tale
description: A whale breaches the surface of the ocean, revealing a hidden cove where a group of people are enjoying a relaxing day.  The scene transitions to show a Bridgestone tire smoothly navigating a winding road. The ad emphasizes the tire's reliability and performance, highlighting the connection between a smooth driving experience and a peaceful, natural setting.  The whale's majestic appearance juxtaposes with the precision engineering implied by the tire's capability.

title: Sumo Wrestling
description: The 2010 KGB Super Bowl ad depicts a humorous sumo wrestling match between two large men.  The match is unexpectedly interrupted by a smaller man who skillfully uses KGB's presumably superior vodka to incapacitate the larger wrestlers. The smaller man emerges victorious, highlighting the vodka's potency and unexpected strength in a comedic manner. The ad features minimal dialogue and relies on visual humor and slapstick to convey its message.

title: Baby Girlfriend
description: The 2010 ETRADE Super Bowl ad, "Baby Girlfriend," features a man comically obsessed with his baby daughter, mistaking her for his girlfriend.  He pampers her excessively, showcasing his dedication and highlighting the ad's message of prioritizing family and financial planning for the future. The humor comes from the juxtaposition of romantic gestures towards a baby, ending with the E*TRADE baby logo.

title: Baby First Class
description: A baby is shown luxuriously enjoying first-class amenities on a plane, including a personal attendant and gourmet meals.  The ad contrasts this opulent experience with the everyday struggles of parents.  The punchline reveals that ETRADE makes investing easy, allowing parents to potentially afford such luxuries for their children in the future. The baby's contented expression and the juxtaposition with parental stress form the humor.

title: Little KISS
description: The 2010 Dr Pepper Super Bowl commercial, "Little KISS," features miniature versions of the KISS band members performing a comedically scaled-down version of their usual extravagant stage show.  The tiny KISS members, complete with miniature instruments and costumes,  play in front of a miniature crowd and even utilize miniature pyrotechnics. The ad emphasizes the unexpected and playful nature of Dr Pepper.

title: Baby Tears
description: The ETRADE 2010 Super Bowl commercial, "Baby Tears," features a baby crying uncontrollably.  A voiceover explains that the baby's tears are caused by the stress of financial planning.  The ad then showcases ETRADE's services as a solution, implying that using their platform eliminates financial anxieties. The baby's tears eventually stop, symbolizing relief and successful financial management with ETRADE.

title: Megan Fox Blur
description: The 2010 Motorola Super Bowl ad features Megan Fox in a stylized, fast-paced montage.  Blurred images and quick cuts showcase her in various scenarios, emphasizing the speed and advanced technology of Motorola's then-new phone.  The ad's core message highlights the phone's ability to capture life's fleeting moments with clear, high-quality imagery, contrasting the blur of motion with the phone's sharp clarity.  The overall tone is sleek and modern, using Fox's celebrity appeal to draw attention to the product.

title: Auto Tune with TPain
original_title: 2010 BUD LIGHT – Auto Tune with TPain
description: The 2010 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial features T-Pain using auto-tune to hilariously transform ordinary situations into catchy songs.  The ad showcases several scenarios: a man proposing, a group of friends playing beer pong, and a woman receiving flowers.  T-Pain's auto-tune enhances these moments, turning mundane dialogue into comedic, musical interludes, ultimately promoting Bud Light beer.

title: Eager Beaver
description: The 2010 Monster.com Super Bowl ad, "Eager Beaver," depicts a highly enthusiastic, almost manic beaver relentlessly applying for jobs.  He uses various methods, from a high-tech resume delivery system to extreme measures like attaching his resume to a rocket.  The ad highlights Monster.com's job search capabilities through the beaver's over-the-top dedication to finding employment.  The humor lies in the juxtaposition of the beaver's extreme actions with the everyday reality of job hunting.

title: Asteroid
description: The Bud Light Super Bowl 2010 commercial, titled "Asteroid," depicts a group of friends enjoying a night out.  A sudden, unexpected asteroid shower begins, causing chaos and destruction.  The friends, however, remain remarkably calm and unfazed, continuing to drink Bud Light as the world around them crumbles. The ad uses humor to highlight the resilience and carefree attitude associated with the beer brand, implying that even in apocalyptic situations, Bud Light remains a reliable companion.

title: Casual Friday
description: The CareerBuilder.com Super Bowl ad from 2010, titled "Casual Friday," humorously depicts a series of office workers engaging in increasingly bizarre and inappropriate "casual Friday" attire.  The scenes include a man dressed as a chimpanzee, another wearing a full-body chicken suit, and a woman in a bizarre, furry costume. The absurdity highlights the potential consequences of poorly defined dress codes and a lack of workplace professionalism. The ad concludes with the CareerBuilder.com logo and website address.

title: PunchDub
description: The 2010 Volkswagen PunchDub Super Bowl commercial features a group of Volkswagen Beetles engaging in a playful, choreographed dance routine in a parking lot.  The upbeat music and synchronized movements highlight the car's maneuverability and quirky personality.  The ad concludes with the Volkswagen logo and tagline, emphasizing the fun and spirited nature of the vehicle.

title: The Last Airbender
description: The advertisement is a trailer for the 2010 film adaptation of 'Avatar: The Last Airbender'.  It showcases quick cuts of action scenes, featuring the main characters Aang, Katara, and Sokka, and glimpses of fantastical elements from the world of the show. The trailer aims to generate excitement and anticipation for the movie's release, highlighting the visually stunning world and the adventure that awaits.

title: The Game with Betty White and Abe Vigoda
original_title: 2010 SNICKERS – The Game with Betty White and Abe Vigoda
description: The ad shows a football game where two elderly players, Betty White and Abe Vigoda, are playing aggressively.  Their behavior is unusual and eventually revealed to be due to hunger. A younger player offers them a Snickers bar, and after eating it, they revert to their normal, pleasant selves. The ad highlights the idea that hunger can cause drastic changes in personality and that Snickers can resolve this.

title: Shock Collar
description: A man is walking his dog when the dog runs off.  He uses a remote-controlled shock collar to get the dog's attention, but accidentally shocks a squirrel, a bird, and finally, a group of people on a park bench.  The humor lies in the escalating consequences of his misdirected shock. The ad ends with the tagline "Doritos: For when you're hungry for something more." It focuses on the unexpected and humorous outcomes rather than directly showcasing the product.

title: 2020 MVP with Brett Favre
description: The 2010 Hyundai Super Bowl commercial features Brett Favre, the then-recently retired NFL quarterback.  The ad uses a humorous approach, showing Favre's supposed struggles with retirement, like attempting to learn a new skill—juggling.  He ultimately finds success with his new Hyundai Genesis Coupe, showcasing the car's sporty features.  The overall message is that even a legendary athlete can find a new passion and enjoy the drive in a Hyundai.

title: My Generation
description: The 2010 FLOTV Super Bowl ad, "My Generation," uses a montage of iconic moments and cultural touchstones from the past to present, set to a driving rock soundtrack.  It rapidly flashes images representing various eras and trends, showcasing technological advancements, fashion changes, social shifts, and popular culture references. The overall message centers on the evolution of generations and the enduring spirit of youth and rebellion.  There's no clear product demonstration, rather the ad focuses on brand association with cultural zeitgeist.

title: Green Police
description: The 2010 Audi Super Bowl ad, "Green Police," depicts a futuristic scenario where environmentally conscious police officers patrol a city in sleek, electric Audi vehicles.  They meticulously enforce green initiatives, such as ensuring proper recycling and preventing pollution. The ad showcases the cars' advanced technology and eco-friendly features, highlighting Audi's commitment to sustainability. The tone is lighthearted and humorous, contrasting the serious message of environmental responsibility with a playful enforcement approach.

title: The Journey
description: The 2010 Gatorade Super Bowl commercial, "The Journey," follows a young boy's intense football practice montage, interspersed with shots of him drinking Gatorade.  It emphasizes hard work, dedication, and perseverance, culminating in the boy triumphantly scoring a touchdown. The ad uses slow-motion shots and inspirational music to build excitement and connect Gatorade with athletic achievement.

title: I Wear No Pants
description: The 2010 Dockers Super Bowl ad, "I Wear No Pants," features a man confidently navigating various social situations while seemingly wearing no pants.  The humorous premise plays on the comfortable and stylish nature of Dockers pants.  The ad showcases the man in various settings – a coffee shop, a party, etc. – always maintaining a composed demeanor despite the comedic absurdity of his lack of pants. The focus is on the comfort and versatility of the pants, suggesting they are suitable for any occasion.

title: Body Pass
description: The 2010 Hyundai Super Bowl commercial, "Body Pass," showcases a football player's impressive agility and skill as he makes a series of incredible catches and passes, using his body to maneuver the ball.  The ad emphasizes the Hyundai's maneuverability and control, subtly linking the player's athleticism to the car's performance.  It concludes with the Hyundai logo and tagline. The focus is on demonstrating the vehicle's handling through a visually striking, athletic metaphor.

title: Robin Hood
description: The 2010 Miramax Super Bowl ad for the film "Robin Hood" features quick cuts of action scenes from the movie.  We see Russell Crowe as Robin Hood, fighting, riding horses, and engaging in archery.  The overall tone is intense and dramatic, showcasing the film's adventurous and action-packed nature.  The ad effectively uses cinematic visuals to highlight the movie's key elements and generate excitement.

title: The Wolfman
description: The Super Bowl ad for Universal Pictures' 2010 film "The Wolfman" is a darkly atmospheric trailer showcasing scenes of suspense and horror.  It features glimpses of Benicio del Toro as Lawrence Talbot transforming into a werewolf, interspersed with shots of menacing figures and a moonlit forest. The trailer relies heavily on visual storytelling and sound design to build a sense of dread and anticipation for the film's release, emphasizing its gothic horror elements.

title: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter
original_title: 2010 UNIVERSAL ORLANDO – The Wizarding World of Harry Potter
description: The 2010 Universal Orlando Super Bowl ad showcases the then-new Wizarding World of Harry Potter at Universal Studios Florida.  The commercial uses quick cuts of exciting scenes from the park, including Hogwarts castle, the flight of the hippogriff, and various shops and rides. It emphasizes the immersive and magical experience offered, highlighting the realism and attention to detail in recreating the world of Harry Potter. The ad aims to generate excitement and encourage viewers to visit the theme park.

title: Best Fans on the Planet
original_title: 2010 NFL – Best Fans on the Planet
description: The 2010 NFL Super Bowl ad, "Best Fans on the Planet," showcases diverse and enthusiastic football fans from various backgrounds and locations.  The commercial features quick cuts of fans cheering, tailgating, and celebrating, emphasizing the unifying power of the NFL and the passion of its fanbase.  It highlights different fan demographics and experiences, from families to individuals, in stadiums and at home, creating a vibrant and energetic portrayal of NFL fandom.

title: Awesomer
description: The 2010 Pop Secret Emerald Nuts Super Bowl commercial features a series of absurd and humorous scenarios.  A man dramatically announces the awesomeness of Pop Secret Emerald Nuts while various comedic situations unfold, including a man dramatically catching a falling microwave, people reacting with exaggerated joy to the popcorn, and a bizarre sequence involving a man in a suit and a small dog. The overall tone is lighthearted and silly, focusing on the unexpected delight of the product.

title: Alice in Wonderland
description: The 2010 Super Bowl Disney ad for Alice in Wonderland features quick cuts of scenes from the movie, showcasing the fantastical world, characters like Alice, the Mad Hatter, and the Queen of Hearts.  It emphasizes the film's whimsical nature and visual spectacle with a fast-paced montage.  The ad doesn't have a clear narrative but aims to generate excitement and anticipation for the movie release.  The overall tone is bright, colorful, and magical.

title: Go To Hell
description: The 2010 Super Bowl ad for Dante's Inferno video game depicts a chaotic, action-packed scene of hellish landscapes and demonic figures.  It showcases intense gameplay footage with fast-paced combat and supernatural elements.  The ad relies heavily on the game's visual spectacle to convey its violent and fantastical nature, aiming to excite viewers with its dark fantasy setting.

title: Squirrel
description: The 2010 Honda Crosstour Super Bowl commercial features a squirrel repeatedly thwarting a man's attempts to retrieve his misplaced keys.  The squirrel uses the keys to unlock and enter the Crosstour, eventually driving off, leaving the man bewildered. The ad uses slapstick humor to showcase the vehicle's features, particularly its keyless entry system, in a light-hearted and memorable way.  The overall tone is comedic and focuses on the unexpected actions of the squirrel.

title: Up
description: The Super Bowl ad for Disney Pixar's Up shows a montage of heartwarming scenes from the movie.  It highlights the adventurous spirit of Carl Fredricksen and Russell, their journey to South America, and the emotional bond between them.  The ad uses uplifting music and quick cuts to evoke the film's whimsical and touching aspects, ultimately promoting the film's release.

title: Contract
description: The 2009 Hyundai Assurance Super Bowl commercial depicts a man signing a contract with a devilish-looking representative.  The contract seemingly grants the man incredible good fortune, but with a twist.  He experiences a series of seemingly improbable lucky events—winning a lottery, finding money, and avoiding accidents. However, the final scene reveals the 'devil' was actually a Hyundai Assurance representative and his good fortune was insurance-related, suggesting Hyundai Assurance protects against unforeseen events.

title: 1 Second Ad- Super Bowl Ad
original_title: 2009 MILLER HIGH LIFE – 1 Second Ad- Super Bowl Ad
description: The Miller High Life Super Bowl ad from 2009 is a single-second spot.  It shows a single bottle of Miller High Life champagne-style beer dramatically appearing in a spotlight against a dark background.  The bottle is presented with an emphasis on its elegant, tall shape and the brand's logo is prominently displayed. No other elements or actions are shown.  It relies on the inherent brand recognition and sophistication implied by the product to make its statement within this ultra-short timeframe.

title: Hot Item
description: The 2009 Bridgestone Super Bowl commercial, titled "Hot Item," depicts a series of humorous scenarios where everyday objects—a hot dog, a bowling ball, and a cell phone—unexpectedly become projectiles, highlighting the unexpected situations drivers may encounter.  The ad emphasizes the importance of reliable tires, implying that Bridgestone tires can handle these unpredictable events.  The commercial concludes with the Bridgestone logo and tagline.

title: Sheep
description: The 2009 Bridgestone Super Bowl ad, titled "Sheep," depicts a flock of sheep meticulously following a lead sheep, even as it makes seemingly illogical turns.  The lead sheep is revealed to be driving a car, showcasing the tire's exceptional handling and control, even in challenging, unpredictable circumstances. The ad emphasizes the reliable performance and precision of Bridgestone tires through this unusual and memorable metaphor.

title: Heeeres Money
description: The 2009 CASH 4 GOLD Super Bowl commercial, titled "Heeeres Money," features a man dressed as Elvis Presley enthusiastically promoting the company's gold buying services.  He sings and dances, showcasing various ways people can bring in gold to receive cash. The ad uses bright colors and rapid cuts to create an energetic and memorable impression. The Elvis impersonator's over-the-top performance is the central focus, emphasizing the ease and profitability of selling gold to CASH 4 GOLD.

title: Angry Bosses
description: The 2009 Hyundai Super Bowl ad, "Angry Bosses," features a series of exasperated bosses reacting comically to various employee shortcomings.  The humor stems from their over-the-top reactions, such as throwing phones and dramatically sighing.  The advertisement subtly promotes Hyundai vehicles by showing the employees driving away in them after work, implying freedom and escape from stressful work environments.  The overall tone is lighthearted and comedic, focusing on relatable workplace frustrations.

title: Mean Troy
description: The 2009 Coke Zero Super Bowl ad, "Mean Troy," features a seemingly menacing, muscular man named Troy who aggressively approaches people only to reveal a surprisingly gentle and friendly demeanor after he takes a sip of Coke Zero.  The ad uses humor to contrast his intimidating appearance with his kind actions.  He offers people Coke Zero and their reactions range from surprised to delighted. The ad ends with Troy's transformation completely portrayed, showcasing the drink's effect on his personality.

title: Heist
description: The 2009 Coca-Cola Super Bowl ad, "Heist," depicts a playful robbery of a Coca-Cola truck. A group of quirky characters, including a young boy, meticulously plan and execute the theft, showcasing their teamwork and lighthearted camaraderie.  The heist itself is a series of comical mishaps and near misses, ultimately culminating in a shared celebratory moment of drinking Coke with the truck's driver. The ad emphasizes fun, friendship, and the simple pleasure of enjoying a Coca-Cola.

title: Avatar
description: The 2009 Coca-Cola Super Bowl ad, themed around the movie Avatar, depicts a futuristic, vibrant setting.  It shows Na'vi characters interacting with humans, sharing a Coca-Cola. The ad emphasizes unity and shared experiences, highlighting the universal appeal of Coca-Cola, even across vastly different cultures and worlds.  It uses stunning visuals mirroring the film's aesthetic to create a sense of wonder and adventure.

title: Plant a Seed
description: The 2009 Kellogg's Super Bowl ad, "Plant a Seed," showcases a young boy's journey from planting a seed to harvesting a crop.  The ad emphasizes the growth and nurturing aspect, paralleling the growth of children and families.  It features heartwarming scenes of family life and the simple joys of working together.  The overall message is one of family, growth, and the wholesome nature of Kellogg's products, subtly connecting the act of planting a seed to the consumption of their cereals.

title: Skier
description: The 2009 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial "Skier" depicts a man skiing down a mountain, encountering various humorous obstacles and near-misses.  He expertly navigates treacherous terrain, narrowly avoiding trees and cliffs, all while maintaining a relaxed demeanor and enjoying a Bud Light.  The humor comes from the exaggerated situations and the skier's nonchalant attitude, culminating in a final, successful run. The ad focuses on the enjoyment and carefree nature associated with the Bud Light brand.

title: Power of the Crunch
description: The 2009 Doritos Super Bowl commercial, "Power of the Crunch," showcases a series of escalating, humorous scenarios where the satisfying crunch of a Doritos chip triggers unexpected and increasingly absurd chain reactions.  A man crunches a chip, causing a nearby satellite dish to explode. This then triggers a series of increasingly outlandish events, culminating in a comical, large-scale destruction. The ad emphasizes the irresistible and powerful nature of the chip's crunch.

title: LMAO
description: The 2009 NBC Super Bowl ad, titled "LMAO," is a comedic montage of various clips showcasing humorous and unexpected moments from NBC's programming.  It rapidly cuts between scenes of sitcoms, dramas, news broadcasts, and sports highlights, interspersing them with comedic sound effects and quick cuts.  The overall effect is a fast-paced, laugh-inducing whirlwind of NBC's diverse content, aiming to associate the network with entertainment and fun.

title: Crystal Ball
description: A man uses a crystal ball to predict the future, showcasing various humorous and improbable scenarios.  The predictions involve a romantic encounter, a bizarre party, and a dramatic car chase, all culminating in the man sharing a bag of Doritos with a beautiful woman. The humor lies in the unexpected and absurd nature of the predictions, highlighting the enjoyment derived from sharing Doritos.

title: Tips
description: The 2009 CareerBuilder Super Bowl ad features a series of humorous vignettes showcasing absurd job interview scenarios.  A man brings his pet monkey to the interview, another candidate wears a full suit of armor, and a third arrives in a clown costume.  The overall message is to avoid unprofessional behavior during job interviews.  The ads concludes with the CareerBuilder logo and website address.

title: Alec is Alien, In Hollywood
original_title: 2009 HULU – Alec is Alien, In Hollywood
description: The Hulu Super Bowl ad from 2009 features Alec Baldwin as an alien disguised as a human in Hollywood.  He navigates various stereotypical Hollywood scenarios, including a pretentious party and a movie set.  The humor relies on the contrast between Baldwin's deadpan delivery and the absurdity of his situation, highlighting the vast library of content available on Hulu, implying viewers can find anything they desire, even alien adventures.

title: Talking Baby
description: The 2009 E*TRADE Super Bowl commercial features a baby sitting in a high chair, articulately discussing the complexities of the stock market and financial planning.  He uses adult language and sophisticated financial terms, creating a humorous contrast between his age and his wisdom.  The baby's unexpectedly mature commentary is the ad's central comedic element, promoting ETRADE's services by implying anyone can easily navigate the stock market with their help.

title: I’m Good
description: The 2009 Pepsi Max Super Bowl ad, "I'm Good," features a man confidently asserting "I'm good" in various situations, often defying expectations.  These range from expertly handling a speeding car to nonchalantly extinguishing a fire with a soda. The situations escalate in absurdity, always ending with him calmly saying "I'm Good." The ad uses humor to showcase the confidence Pepsi Max supposedly provides.

title: Meeting
description: The 2009 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Meeting," depicts a tense meeting where executives discuss a new marketing campaign.  The campaign is revealed to be a simple, humorous concept involving a man in a Bud Light costume unexpectedly appearing at various locations. The ad highlights the unexpected and playful nature of the Bud Light brand, contrasting the seriousness of the boardroom with the absurdity of the campaign idea. The focus is on the comedic relief of the situation.

title: Double Take
original_title: 2009 MONSTER.com – Need a New Job – Double Take
description: The 2009 Monster.com Super Bowl ad, "Double Take," features a man unexpectedly encountering various job opportunities throughout his day.  He initially dismisses them, only to realize later their potential.  The scenes are quick cuts showing diverse job settings, emphasizing the wide range of jobs Monster.com offers. The ad ends with the Monster.com logo and tagline, highlighting the ease of finding a new job.

title: Anthem
description: The 2009 Pepsi Super Bowl ad, "Anthem," features a diverse group of individuals from various walks of life – a construction worker, a student, an office worker, etc. – all singing and dancing along to a catchy, upbeat song.  The ad emphasizes unity and shared joy, with people of all ages and backgrounds joining in.  The Pepsi logo is prominently displayed throughout, associating the brand with positive energy and togetherness.  The overall message promotes a sense of community and connection through the shared experience of music and the enjoyment of Pepsi.

title: Speed Date
description: The 2009 Taco Bell Super Bowl ad, "Speed Date," portrays a rapid-fire series of comedic speed dating encounters.  Each date quickly dissolves into chaos as the participants reveal unusual quirks and preferences, ultimately culminating in everyone finding common ground over a shared love for Taco Bell. The ad uses quick cuts, slapstick humor, and exaggerated reactions to create a funny and memorable experience showcasing the brand's accessibility and appeal.

title: Serious Breakfast
description: The 2009 Denny's Super Bowl commercial, "Serious Breakfast," features a diverse group of people enjoying a hearty breakfast at Denny's.  The ad emphasizes the restaurant's atmosphere and abundant food options, showcasing various breakfast items like pancakes, eggs, and bacon.  It uses a fast-paced montage style, highlighting the energy and enjoyment of the diners. The overall message promotes Denny's as a place for a satisfying and fulfilling breakfast experience.

title: Clydesdale Plays Fetch
description: A Budweiser Clydesdale horse is shown enjoying a playful game of fetch with a little girl in a rural setting.  The ad emphasizes the heartwarming bond between the horse and the child, highlighting the idyllic imagery associated with Budweiser. The commercial concludes with the Budweiser logo and tagline.

title: Lizard Lake
description: The 2009 SOBE Lizard Lake Super Bowl commercial features a vibrant, surreal landscape populated by lizards.  A man, seemingly in a desert-like setting, encounters various lizard-like creatures. The scene shifts between shots of the lizards and the man, showcasing the drink's association with a fantastical, otherworldly environment.  The overall tone is whimsical and lighthearted, with no clear narrative beyond the presentation of the product and its quirky imagery.  The ad concludes with a shot of the SOBE drink.

title: New Flavor Pitch
description: The 2009 Doritos Super Bowl commercial, "New Flavor Pitch," showcases a series of humorous scenarios where people try out a new Doritos flavor.  The ad features everyday individuals in unexpected situations, reacting to the chip's taste with exaggerated expressions and quirky actions.  The focus is on the chip's unique and supposedly delicious flavor, creating a lighthearted and comedic atmosphere. The commercial ends with a tagline emphasizing the new flavor.

title: Clydesdales Generations
description: The Budweiser Clydesdales Generations Super Bowl ad shows the evolution of the iconic Clydesdale horses through the years.  It begins with a foal and follows its lineage through several generations, showcasing their training and participation in various parades and Budweiser events.  The ad emphasizes the longevity and tradition associated with both the horses and the Budweiser brand, ending with a shot of a current team pulling a Budweiser wagon. The overall tone is heartwarming and nostalgic.

title: Crazy Pets
description: The 2009 Pedigree Super Bowl commercial, "Crazy Pets," showcases a series of funny and quirky pets engaging in unusual behaviors.  A cat plays the piano, a dog rides a Roomba, and other animals exhibit comical antics. The overall tone is lighthearted and focuses on the playful and unpredictable nature of pets, implicitly connecting this to the enjoyment of owning a Pedigree-fed pet. The ad ends with a shot of various happy pets enjoying Pedigree food.

title: Death and Taxes
description: The 2009 H&R Block Super Bowl ad, "Death and Taxes," uses dark humor to illustrate the inevitability of taxes.  It opens with a grim reaper-like figure collecting taxes from various historical figures, including Cleopatra and a caveman. The ad emphasizes that while death is unavoidable, H&R Block can help individuals navigate the complexities of tax preparation, making it less daunting.

title: Talking Flowers
description: The 2009 Teleflora Super Bowl commercial, "Talking Flowers," features animated flowers that come to life and interact with a woman.  A bouquet of flowers magically springs to life after being delivered. They sing and dance, showcasing the beauty and joy Teleflora brings.  The commercial emphasizes the emotional impact of receiving flowers, portraying a heartwarming and whimsical moment.

title: David Abernathy Confidence
description: The 2009 Cars.com Super Bowl ad features David Abernathy, a seemingly ordinary man, exuding unexpected confidence as he navigates various life situations.  The commercial uses comedic juxtaposition, showing him confidently handling situations like a flat tire and a difficult job interview, all while emphasizing the ease of car searching with Cars.com.  The ad's humor lies in the contrast between Abernathy's outwardly meek demeanor and his surprisingly assertive actions, highlighting the empowering effect of having the right tool (Cars.com) for the job.

title: Spoiled with Chester the Cheetah
original_title: 2009 CHEETOS – Spoiled with Chester the Cheetah
description: The 2009 Cheetos Super Bowl commercial features Chester Cheetah spoiling a young boy rotten with an extravagant amount of Cheetos.  The boy, initially thrilled, becomes increasingly overwhelmed by the sheer volume of Cheetos, eventually resorting to desperate measures – like using them as building blocks – to cope with the cheesy abundance. The ad highlights the addictive and playful nature of Cheetos.

title: Wind Energy
description: The 2009 GE Super Bowl ad showcases the power and potential of wind energy.  It features sweeping shots of wind turbines in various landscapes, emphasizing their scale and environmental impact.  The ad uses uplifting music and minimal narration, focusing on the visual spectacle of the turbines harnessing wind power.  It subtly conveys a message of clean energy and technological advancement without explicitly mentioning specific GE products beyond the brand logo.

title: Napoleon
description: The Garmin Napoleon Super Bowl ad from 2008 uses historical reenactment to showcase the navigation capabilities of its GPS devices.  It depicts Napoleon Bonaparte and his army navigating a seemingly impossible terrain, successfully reaching their destination thanks to a Garmin GPS device. The humor comes from the juxtaposition of historical figures with modern technology, implying that even Napoleon would have benefited from Garmin's precision.

title: Obstacles
description: The 2008 Bridgestone Super Bowl ad, "Obstacles," depicts a series of challenging driving scenarios – a steep, winding mountain road, a narrow, icy path, and a bumpy, off-road terrain.  A driver skillfully navigates these obstacles with the help of Bridgestone tires. The ad emphasizes the tires' ability to handle various difficult driving conditions, showcasing their grip, durability, and performance. The visuals are dynamic and action-oriented, focusing on the car's movements and the tire's performance rather than featuring any people or specific dialogue.

title: Wine & Cheese Party
description: The Bud Light "Wine & Cheese Party" Super Bowl ad from 2008 depicts a group of sophisticated individuals enjoying a wine and cheese party.  Their refined atmosphere is disrupted by the arrival of a group of Bud Light-drinking, boisterous friends, who ultimately convert the wine and cheese enthusiasts to their more casual, fun-loving style. The ad highlights the contrast between pretentiousness and genuine enjoyment, subtly promoting Bud Light as the drink of choice for good times and uninhibited fun.

title: Game is Over
description: The 2008 Victoria's Secret Super Bowl ad, "Game is Over," features several models in lingerie playfully interacting with football players.  The models playfully 'dominate' the football game, ultimately 'winning' against the athletes.  The ad uses a playful, suggestive tone and highlights the lingerie as the focus, with the football game serving as a backdrop.

title: Witch Doctor
description: The 2008 Cars.com Super Bowl ad, "Witch Doctor," features a man seeking a car.  He consults a witch doctor who performs a ritual involving various car parts.  The witch doctor's incantations and actions are comedically exaggerated, culminating in the man receiving a Cars.com website printout. The ad emphasizes Cars.com as the resource for finding a suitable car.

title: Every Sip with Justin Timberlake
original_title: 2008 PEPSI – Every Sip with Justin Timberlake
description: The 2008 Pepsi Super Bowl ad features Justin Timberlake enjoying Pepsi in various settings.  The commercial intercuts shots of him drinking Pepsi with scenes of people enjoying themselves at a party, a concert, and other lively events. The overall mood is upbeat and celebratory, emphasizing the refreshing and enjoyable aspects of the drink. Timberlake's presence adds a star quality, making it a memorable and catchy commercial focused on connecting Pepsi with fun and social experiences.

title: Dalmatian Trains “Hank” for Team
description: A Budweiser Clydesdale horse, Hank, is being trained by a team of Dalmatian puppies. The ad shows the puppies playfully interacting with Hank, teaching him tricks and eventually leading him in a Budweiser parade. The focus is on the heartwarming and humorous interactions between the animals, showcasing the camaraderie and teamwork implied through the training process.  The ad ends with the familiar Budweiser imagery and logo.

title: Mouse Trap
description: A man meticulously sets up an elaborate mousetrap, only to have it backfire hilariously.  The trap, constructed with various household items, is triggered unexpectedly by a cat, sending the man sprawling.  The final shot reveals a bag of Doritos, implying the man's efforts were ultimately for a snack. The humor derives from the elaborate setup and the anticlimactic, unexpected outcome.

title: Carmen Electra
description: The 2008 Ice Breakers Super Bowl commercial features Carmen Electra in various humorous scenarios where she uses Ice Breakers mints to freshen her breath.  The situations are exaggerated and comedic, highlighting the mint's ability to handle various breath-freshening challenges.  The ad relies on Electra's celebrity appeal and uses quick cuts and playful music to maintain a lighthearted tone.

title: Derek Jeter
description: The 2008 Gatorade G2 commercial features Derek Jeter, a renowned baseball player.  The ad opens with Jeter intensely focused, practicing his swing.  It emphasizes his dedication and hard work through quick cuts of training montages.  The ad subtly highlights Gatorade G2 as a part of his regimen, suggesting it contributes to his success and performance.  The overall tone is aspirational, connecting the brand with peak athletic achievement and perseverance.

title: X-Ray Vision
description: The Bud Light Super Bowl XLII commercial, "X-Ray Vision," features a man gaining the ability to see through clothes using X-ray vision after drinking a Bud Light.  He uses this newfound ability to hilariously assess the attractiveness of various women at a bar and to judge the quality of a man's beer selection. The humor lies in the absurdity of the situation and the man's increasingly inappropriate behavior.

title: Ability To Fly
description: The 2008 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Ability to Fly," showcases a man gaining the power of flight after drinking a Bud Light.  He effortlessly soars through various scenarios, including a crowded bar, a baseball game, and a traffic jam.  The ad emphasizes the unexpected and liberating feeling associated with the beer, using whimsical visuals and playful situations to highlight the lightheartedness of the brand.

title: Talking Stain
description: The 2008 Tide To Go commercial features a talking stain on a man's shirt narrating his journey through various social situations.  The stain, with a distinct personality, comments on the man's activities, highlighting the embarrassing scenarios caused by the stain.  The commercial showcases the ease and effectiveness of Tide To Go in removing the stain, culminating in the stain's disappearance and a relieved sigh from the man.

title: Carrier Pigeons
description: The FedEx commercial depicts a historical reenactment where a company uses carrier pigeons to deliver packages. However, a FedEx delivery truck arrives at the destination unexpectedly faster.  The humor arises from the contrast between the outdated method (carrier pigeons) and the superior speed and efficiency of FedEx. The scene concludes with a humorous shot of the pigeons looking surprised by the truck's arrival.

title: Political Parties
description: The 2008 Coca-Cola Super Bowl ad depicts a diverse group of people from different political parties – Democrats and Republicans –  coming together and sharing Coca-Cola.  The ad emphasizes unity and common ground, contrasting the political divide with the simple shared pleasure of enjoying a Coke. It features everyday people in various settings, enjoying the beverage and connecting with one another, suggesting that despite political differences, there are shared human experiences.

title: Pandas
description: The 2008 Salesgenie.com Super Bowl ad features two pandas in a bamboo forest, seemingly oblivious to the chaos around them.  A voiceover explains that Salesgenie.com helps businesses find sales leads, implying that the pandas' calm amidst the storm represents the ease and efficiency of the platform.  The ad uses quirky visuals and a humorous tone to highlight the benefits of the service, contrasting the relaxed pandas with the busy world of sales.

title: Tow Truck Jump
original_title: 2008 AMP ENERGY DRINK – Tow Truck Jump
description: The 2008 AMP Energy Drink Super Bowl ad features a tow truck attempting a daring jump over a series of obstacles.  The jump is shown in slow motion with dramatic music. While the initial attempts fail spectacularly, culminating in the truck crashing, the final jump is successful, showcasing the energy drink's supposed ability to fuel extreme feats. The ad emphasizes the energy drink's power and connection to adrenaline-fueled activities.

title: Wheel Suck
description: The 2008 Bud Light Super Bowl ad, "Wheel Suck," features a group of friends enjoying a Bud Light at a party.  One friend, attempting a party trick, gets his car wheel stuck in a drain.  The humorous scene depicts the friends' reactions and their continued enjoyment of Bud Light despite the unexpected situation. The ad emphasizes casual camaraderie and the drink's association with fun times among friends.  The focus is primarily on the humorous predicament and the lightheartedness of the overall scenario.

title: Thirsty Dog
description: A parched dog, initially portrayed as lethargic and listless, is revitalized after consuming Gatorade G2.  The advertisement uses humorous visual gags, showing the dog's transformation from a drooping, dehydrated state to energetic exuberance after drinking the beverage. The humor is derived from the exaggerated depiction of the dog's thirst and subsequent re-energized behavior. The ad focuses primarily on the thirst-quenching capabilities of Gatorade G2.

title: Breathe Fire
description: The 2008 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Breathe Fire," features a group of friends at a bar who discover their Bud Light cans possess the power to breathe fire.  They initially use this ability to impress women, but the flames quickly get out of control, leading to humorous chaos and destruction at the bar.  The ad ends with a shot of the friends, slightly singed, still enjoying their Bud Lights.

title: Shaq Jockey
description: The 2008 Vitamin Water Super Bowl commercial features Shaquille O'Neal as a jockey in a horse race.  The ad uses comedic exaggeration, showing Shaq's enormous size contrasting hilariously with his petite horse and the other jockeys.  The humor lies in the absurdity of the situation and Shaq's surprisingly graceful, albeit improbable, riding style. The ad ends with Shaq winning the race and taking a celebratory swig of Vitamin Water.

title: Jackie Moon (Will Ferrell)
description: The 2008 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial features Will Ferrell as Jackie Moon, the flamboyant owner and player of the fictional ABA basketball team, the Flint Tropics.  The ad showcases Moon's over-the-top personality and highlights his team's antics, interspersed with shots of people enjoying Bud Light.  The humor relies on Moon's eccentric behavior and the absurdity of the situations, ultimately promoting the beer as a fun and entertaining beverage.

title: Thrillicious
description: The 2008 SOBE Life Water Super Bowl ad, titled "Thrillicious," features a series of surreal and humorous vignettes.  A man experiences increasingly bizarre and escalating events, such as a giant hand reaching from the sky and a flock of birds carrying him away, all while enjoying his SOBE Life Water.  The overall tone is lighthearted and fantastical, emphasizing the unexpected and thrilling aspects of life, enhanced by the drink.

title: Scream
description: The 2008 Bridgestone Super Bowl ad, "Scream," features a man driving a car at high speed down a mountain road, narrowly avoiding a collision with an oncoming truck.  The intense situation and near-miss are emphasized by dramatic music and sound effects. The driver's reaction is one of relief and exhilaration after safely navigating the perilous turn, highlighting the performance and safety of Bridgestone tires. The ad concludes with the Bridgestone logo.

title: It’s Mine
description: The 2008 Coca-Cola Super Bowl ad, "It's Mine," depicts a playful tug-of-war over a Coca-Cola between a young boy and a girl.  The scene unfolds in a park, highlighting the refreshing nature of the drink on a hot day.  The children's playful competition emphasizes the simple pleasure and shared enjoyment associated with Coca-Cola.  The ad ends with both sharing the drink, underlining the unifying feeling Coke evokes.

title: Head Nod
description: The 2008 Diet Pepsi Max Super Bowl ad, "Head Nod," features a series of seemingly unrelated scenes: a man attempting to parallel park, a woman applying makeup, a man eating a sandwich, and others.  Each scene concludes with someone subtly nodding their head.  The final shot reveals a Diet Pepsi Max can, implying the drink's enjoyable taste is the unifying element behind the seemingly disparate moments and head nods. The commercial relies on humor through its juxtaposition of random scenes and a shared subtle action.

title: R8
description: The 2008 Audi R8 Super Bowl commercial showcases the car's sleek design and powerful performance.  The ad features dramatic visuals of the R8 speeding down a winding road at night, emphasizing its handling and speed.  The emphasis is on the car's aesthetic appeal and exhilarating driving experience, with minimal dialogue or other distractions. The video primarily focuses on showcasing the car's capabilities and luxurious design in a visually stunning and dynamic manner.  The overall tone is one of excitement and prestige.

title: Language of Love
description: The Bud Light "Language of Love" Super Bowl ad from 2008 depicts a series of humorous scenarios where couples misinterpret each other's attempts at romantic gestures due to language barriers.  A diverse group of couples are shown in various situations, highlighting the comedic misunderstandings stemming from miscommunication. The ad concludes with a Bud Light toast, suggesting the shared enjoyment of the beer transcends language differences.  The overall tone is lighthearted and playful, focusing on the universal experience of romance and the occasional challenges of communication.

title: Baby Spits Up
description: The 2008 E-TRADE Super Bowl commercial features a baby spitting up on a businessman during a crucial moment in a business meeting. The surprised reactions of the adults are juxtaposed with the baby's nonchalant attitude. The ad uses humor to suggest that even amidst serious business decisions, unexpected interruptions can occur, implying that E-TRADE's services offer convenience and simplicity despite life's chaos.

title: Baby Hires Clown
description: A baby, sitting in a high chair, is frustrated with his investments.  He uses a tablet to fire his financial advisor and then hires a clown as his replacement. The clown performs silly financial advice, like juggling money and blowing bubbles, showcasing the absurdity of some financial services. The ad ends with the E-TRADE baby looking pleased with this unconventional approach, suggesting E-TRADE offers a simpler, less complicated alternative.

title: Office Worker
description: The 2008 Salesgenie.com Super Bowl ad depicts a mundane office environment where employees are frustrated and unproductive.  A sudden burst of energy and excitement ensues after the introduction of Salesgenie.com, transforming their work atmosphere into a vibrant, highly efficient and successful one. The ad emphasizes the software's ability to boost productivity and improve workplace morale. The overall tone is upbeat and positive, highlighting the before-and-after effect of using the software.

title: Generations
description: The Sunsilk Generations ad shows a multi-generational family of women, from grandmother to granddaughter, showcasing the brand's hair care products.  Each woman is depicted in a different era, highlighting changing styles and trends over time, while emphasizing the consistent use of Sunsilk. The ad emphasizes the longevity of the brand and its connection to female beauty across generations.

title: Stars Sing Chevy Songs
description: The 2007 Chevrolet Super Bowl ad features various celebrities singing modified versions of classic Chevy-themed songs.  The ad is a lighthearted, upbeat montage of short clips showing each celebrity singing their respective lines, intercut with shots of Chevrolet vehicles.  The celebrities appear to be enjoying themselves, and the overall tone is positive and celebratory, associating the brand with fun and familiarity.

title: Training Seminar
description: The CareerBuilder Super Bowl ad from 2007 depicts a hilariously inept corporate training seminar.  The employees, dressed in business attire, participate in increasingly absurd exercises, including an awkward 'trust fall' and a bizarre team-building activity involving a goat and a human pyramid. The humor derives from the awkwardness and absurdity of the situations, highlighting the sometimes-comical nature of corporate training and the disconnect between theory and practice.

title: Survival of the Fittest
description: The 2007 CareerBuilder Super Bowl commercial, "Survival of the Fittest," depicts a series of hilariously inept office workers competing in a corporate survival challenge.  The scenarios involve ridiculous struggles with everyday office tasks, like using a stapler and answering the phone,  ending with the 'winners' celebrating their questionable skills. The humor lies in the contrast between the serious tone of a survival show and the absurdity of the office workers' struggles.

title: Happiness Factory
description: The Coca-Cola Happiness Factory ad depicts a whimsical factory where ingredients like sunshine and laughter are processed to create Coca-Cola.  Workers in the factory joyfully perform tasks, culminating in bottles of Coca-Cola being delivered to happy customers in various scenarios. The overall tone is lighthearted and fantastical, emphasizing the association of Coca-Cola with happiness and positive emotions.

title: Video Game
description: The 2007 Coca-Cola Super Bowl ad depicts a group of diverse individuals, seemingly strangers, bonding over a shared Coke experience.  The ad unfolds as a series of vignettes showing people from different walks of life enjoying Coca-Cola in various settings. It emphasizes the unifying power of the drink, creating a sense of connection and community among people of varying ages and backgrounds. The overall tone is upbeat and positive, celebrating the simple pleasure of sharing a Coke.

title: Check Out Girl
description: A young man is intensely focused on playing a video game at an arcade.  A girl walks by, catching his attention. He tries to subtly check her out without looking too obvious, making exaggerated movements to seemingly adjust his game controls while constantly glancing at her.  His clumsy attempts and the girl's eventual amused reaction are the humor of the ad, culminating in the tagline "Doritos. For those who dare." The video game is a secondary plot device while the focus is on the interaction and the snack food.

title: Live the Favor
description: The 2007 Doritos Super Bowl commercial, "Live the Favor," depicts a series of humorous scenarios where people go to extreme lengths to get a Doritos chip.  A man uses a grappling hook to snag a chip from a high shelf, while another strategically employs a complex pulley system. The ad showcases the irresistible allure of the snack through exaggerated and comedic situations, highlighting the lengths someone will go to for a Doritos chip.

title: One Finger
description: The 2007 E*TRADE Super Bowl commercial, "One Finger," features a chimpanzee sitting at a computer effortlessly trading stocks with one finger.  The chimp's relaxed demeanor contrasts sharply with a stressed-out businessman struggling with complex paperwork. The ad humorously highlights the ease and simplicity of E*TRADE's online trading platform, emphasizing its accessibility even for primates.  The chimp's actions imply that anyone can easily use the platform.

title: Dalmatian
description: The 2007 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial features a Clydesdale horse and a Dalmatian puppy sharing a heartwarming bond.  The puppy playfully follows the horse throughout various settings, culminating in a heartwarming scene where the horse gently nudges the puppy. The ad emphasizes the companionship and loyalty between the animals, subtly linking it to the Budweiser brand.

title: King Crab
description: A majestic king crab, seemingly enjoying a leisurely swim, is shown in various underwater shots.  The crab is then seen scuttling along the ocean floor before finally reaching a Budweiser bottle, which it appears to 'appreciate'. The ad emphasizes the refreshing nature of the beer, linking it to the natural beauty of the ocean environment. The overall tone is calm and serene, with a focus on visually appealing imagery and subtle humor.

title: Don Shula VS JayZ
description: The 2007 Budweiser Super Bowl ad features a comedic showdown between legendary football coach Don Shula and rapper Jay-Z.  The ad plays on the rivalry between football and hip-hop culture.  Shula, in a suit, sits confidently at a bar, while Jay-Z, in his signature attire, enters, attempting to order a Budweiser.  The ensuing back-and-forth is light-hearted and playful, culminating in a humorous exchange about who deserves the Budweiser more. The ad highlights the brand's appeal to diverse audiences.

title: Snickers Kiss
description: The 2007 Snickers Kiss Super Bowl commercial features a romantic scene between a man and a woman on a date.  The man, initially suave and charming, gradually transforms into a less attractive, slobbering, and less appealing version of himself after he takes a bite of the Snickers bar.  The woman's reaction reflects his change in demeanor.  The ad concludes with the tagline emphasizing that a Snickers bar can prevent such unpleasant transformations, implying it keeps you from acting 'like a different person'.

title: Connectile Dysfunction
description: The 2007 Sprint Super Bowl commercial, "Connectile Dysfunction," humorously depicts the frustrations of slow internet connections.  It showcases several scenarios where individuals experience significant delays due to poor connectivity, culminating in missed opportunities and comedic mishaps. The ad emphasizes the speed and reliability of Sprint's network by contrasting it with the sluggishness of competitors' services.  The overall tone is lighthearted and satirical, highlighting the negative impact of slow internet speeds on daily life.

title: But He Has Bud Light
original_title: 2007 BUD LIGHT – But He Has Bud Light
description: The 2007 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial showcases a series of humorous scenarios where a man's possession of Bud Light unexpectedly resolves various conflicts.  A bar fight, a potential romantic rejection, and a tense standoff are all defused simply by the presence of Bud Light.  The ad relies on slapstick humor and quick cuts to create a comedic effect, highlighting the beer as a universal peacemaker.

title: Slap
description: The 2007 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Slap," features a man enjoying a Bud Light at a bar.  A woman unexpectedly slaps him across the face.  He is initially shocked but then smiles, revealing a Bud Light can behind his back. The implication is he orchestrated the slap to cleverly reveal his beer to the audience. The ad ends with the Bud Light tagline.

title: Robot
description: The 2007 GM Super Bowl ad, "Robot," depicts a futuristic scenario where a robot, meticulously assembling a car, is revealed to be a human worker inside a high-tech suit.  The ad showcases GM's advanced manufacturing processes and highlights the precision and skill involved in car production.  The focus is on the technology and human element working together, ending with the GM logo and tagline.

title: Apes Plan
description: The 2007 Bud Light Super Bowl ad, "Apes Plan," features a group of chimpanzees meticulously planning a heist to steal a large quantity of Bud Light.  The apes utilize sophisticated tools and teamwork, showcasing their cunning plan.  The humor lies in the unexpected juxtaposition of intelligent primates executing a complex operation for beer. The ad concludes with the apes successfully achieving their goal.

title: K-Fed, Rollin’ VIP
description: The 2007 Nationwide Super Bowl commercial features Kevin Federline, portraying himself, driving a luxury car and enjoying various VIP perks.  The humor comes from the juxtaposition of his celebrity status with seemingly mundane situations. He's shown receiving overly attentive service, highlighting the contrast between his perceived importance and the everyday experiences.  The ad emphasizes Nationwide's ability to cater to a variety of needs, subtly suggesting they can handle anything, even K-Fed's unique lifestyle.

title: Rock Scissors Paper
description: The Bud Light commercial depicts a bar scene where two men engage in a rock-paper-scissors game for the last Bud Light.  The game is intense and dramatic, with close-ups on their faces and the hand gestures. The stakes are high, the tension builds, and the final outcome is revealed, highlighting the playful rivalry over a beer.

title: Class with Carlos Mencia
original_title: 2007 BUD LIGHT – Class with Carlos Mencia
description: The Bud Light Super Bowl 2007 commercial features comedian Carlos Mencia teaching a class on 'how to be cool.'  The humorous premise involves Mencia's comedic style, using exaggerated scenarios and punchlines about Bud Light and 'coolness.' The ad uses quick cuts and various students reacting to Mencia's 'lessons,' highlighting the brand's association with a relaxed, fun atmosphere. The overall message subtly connects Bud Light with a sense of casual coolness and shared experiences among friends.

title: In the Sun
description: The 2007 IZOD Super Bowl commercial, "In the Sun," features a diverse group of people enjoying various outdoor activities in sunny locations.  The scenes are vibrant and upbeat, showcasing individuals engaged in activities such as surfing, skateboarding, and relaxing on a beach.  The overall tone is positive and aspirational, associating the IZOD brand with a carefree and active lifestyle.  The ad emphasizes the brand's clothing, subtly showcasing IZOD apparel throughout the diverse scenes without explicitly highlighting any specific product features.

title: Quattro Titanium
description: The 2007 Schick Quattro Titanium Super Bowl commercial showcases the razor's features through a series of quick cuts.  It depicts various men in diverse settings—a businessman, a surfer, a construction worker—experiencing smooth, comfortable shaves. The ad emphasizes the razor's four blades and titanium coating, highlighting its ease of use and superior performance.  The overall tone is upbeat and aspirational, associating the product with a confident and active lifestyle.

title: Mouse
description: A frantic mouse scurries through a Blockbuster store, narrowly avoiding capture by a cat.  The mouse's chaotic journey highlights the vast selection of movies available at Blockbuster. The ad culminates with the mouse finding refuge amongst the movie cases, implying the abundant choices available to Blockbuster customers.  The ad uses the mouse's perspective to showcase the store's size and diverse movie collection.

title: Work Smart
description: The 2007 Sales Genie Super Bowl commercial depicts a stressed-out businessman struggling with inefficient sales processes.  He's shown overwhelmed by paperwork and phone calls.  A genie then appears, offering a solution – Sales Genie software. The ad showcases the software's ability to streamline sales tasks, leading to increased efficiency and ultimately, the businessman relaxing and enjoying his success.  The overall tone is one of problem/solution, highlighting the software's ease of use and effectiveness.

title: Lions
description: The 2007 Taco Bell Super Bowl commercial, "Lions," features a group of highly-stylized, CGI lions lounging around a luxurious living room, consuming Taco Bell products with sophisticated manners.  The scene contrasts the expected wildness of lions with their refined enjoyment of fast food, creating a humorous juxtaposition.  The ad concludes with a shot of the Taco Bell logo and tagline.

title: Sheryl Crow
description: The 2007 Revlon Super Bowl ad features Sheryl Crow applying Revlon makeup while singing a snippet of a song.  The setting is elegant and sophisticated.  The focus is on the ease and beauty of the makeup application, subtly showcasing different Revlon products like lipstick and mascara.  Crow's presence adds a touch of glamour and sophistication, associating the brand with a famous and respected artist. The ad ends with a shot of the Revlon logo and tagline.

title: Road of Tomorrow
description: The 2007 Michelin "Road of Tomorrow" Super Bowl ad depicts a futuristic, sleek highway system seamlessly integrating various advanced technologies.  Self-driving cars navigate effortlessly, showcasing the tire's role in enabling this advanced mobility.  The visuals emphasize speed, precision, and the smooth, controlled movement of vehicles, suggesting a vision of effortless and safe future transportation.  The ad is less about specific tire features and more about Michelin's association with innovation and the future of driving.

title: OC Choppers
description: The 2007 HP Super Bowl ad features custom motorcycle builder Jesse James of West Coast Choppers building a motorcycle.  The ad emphasizes the speed and power of HP computers by juxtaposing the creation of the bike with the speed of data processing.  The fast-paced editing and dramatic music highlight the efficiency of HP technology.  The ad concludes with the HP logo and tagline.

title: Maposaurus
description: The 2007 Garmin Maposaurus Super Bowl ad depicts a humorous scene where a prehistoric creature, a Maposaurus, navigates modern-day traffic using a Garmin GPS device. The creature is shown driving a car, successfully using the GPS to avoid obstacles and reach its destination. The ad highlights the GPS's ease of use and reliability even in unusual circumstances, emphasizing its simple and effective navigation capabilities. The commercial is lighthearted and uses humor to showcase the product's functionality.

title: Robert Goulet
description: The 2007 Emerald Nuts Super Bowl commercial features Robert Goulet, the famous singer, unexpectedly appearing in various mundane settings.  He dramatically sings about the deliciousness of Emerald Nuts while people around him react with surprise and amusement.  The ad emphasizes the unexpected delight of enjoying Emerald Nuts, contrasting Goulet's operatic style with everyday situations.

title: Heart Attack
description: The 2007 King Pharmaceuticals Super Bowl ad depicts a series of everyday scenarios where people experience sudden, unexpected heart attacks.  The scenes are interspersed with shots of a single red heart beating rapidly. The ad emphasizes the seriousness of heart attacks and subtly promotes the need for heart health awareness and possibly medication, although no specific product is explicitly advertised. The overall tone is serious and cautionary, driving home the message about heart attack risk.

title: See Saw
description: The 2007 Toyota Tundra Super Bowl commercial, "See Saw," depicts a playful tug-of-war between a Tundra pickup truck and a massive, lumbering dinosaur.  The truck effortlessly wins, showcasing its strength and power.  The scene is set in a whimsical, almost cartoonish landscape, highlighting the Tundra's capability against an absurdly powerful opponent. The ad uses simple visual storytelling, emphasizing the truck's strength and durability.

title: Whopperettes
description: The 2006 Burger King Super Bowl commercial, "Whopperettes," features a group of scantily clad women in roller skates delivering Whopper burgers.  The ad uses suggestive humor and innuendo, playing on the double entendre of "Whopperettes." The women are energetic and perform synchronized skating routines while delivering burgers. The focus is on the playful and suggestive presentation of the product rather than focusing on a detailed explanation of the Whopper itself.

title: Addicted to Lost
description: The 2006 ABC Super Bowl ad for the TV show *Lost* uses a suspenseful, cinematic approach.  It features quick cuts of dramatic scenes from the show, highlighting mysterious elements like the plane crash, the island's strange inhabitants, and the characters' struggles for survival.  The overall tone is intense and intriguing, designed to hook viewers and create anticipation for the upcoming season.  The ad ends with the show's logo and air date.

title: Airplane
description: The AmeriQuest 2006 Super Bowl commercial, titled "Airplane," depicts a series of humorous scenarios involving a man's increasingly absurd attempts to get home.  He tries various methods of transportation, each escalating in silliness, culminating in him literally flying home like Superman. The ad emphasizes the company's commitment to providing solutions, even if unconventional, to help people reach their goals. The overall tone is lighthearted and comedic.

title: Hospital
description: The AmeriQuest Super Bowl 2006 ad depicts a chaotic hospital scene with numerous patients and staff rushing around.  A man is shown repeatedly asking for help, ultimately receiving a simple solution to his problem: AmeriQuest's services to help find better healthcare plans.  The ad uses fast cuts and comedic timing to highlight the stressful experience of navigating the healthcare system before suggesting AmeriQuest as a solution.

title: Magic Fridge
description: The 2006 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Magic Fridge," depicts a man discovering a refrigerator that magically produces various items, including Bud Light.  The fridge grants wishes, such as a party appearing in his living room and a beautiful woman emerging from it. title: Jessica Simpson and the Muppets
original_title: 2004 PIZZA HUT – Jessica Simpson and the Muppets
description: The 2004 Pizza Hut Super Bowl commercial features Jessica Simpson interacting with the Muppets.  Kermit the Frog and Miss Piggy are shown in a Pizza Hut, with Jessica Simpson ordering pizza.  The ad uses humor, with the Muppets' typical comedic antics playing out alongside Simpson's playful participation.  The focus is on Pizza Hut's pizza, showcasing it as a fun, enjoyable food to share.

title: Winter Beach Volleyball with Kerri Walsh and Misty May
original_title: 2004 VISA – Winter Beach Volleyball with Kerri Walsh and Misty May
description: The 2004 Visa commercial features Olympic beach volleyball stars Kerri Walsh and Misty May playing volleyball on a snowy beach in winter.  The ad highlights the convenience and acceptance of Visa cards, showcasing their use in various winter-themed scenarios, such as purchasing hot chocolate and renting skis. The overall message promotes Visa's widespread usability, even in unexpected situations, with a focus on the athletes' playful and energetic personalities.

title: Balcony Jump
description: The 2004 Sierra Mist Super Bowl commercial, "Balcony Jump," depicts a comedic scenario where a man dramatically prepares to jump from a balcony, only to reveal he's simply reaching for a can of Sierra Mist.  The ad emphasizes the refreshing nature of the soda with humorous exaggeration of the man's perceived desperation for a drink. The suspense is quickly deflated for a comedic punchline. The ad's visual style is simple but memorable, relying on the unexpected twist to create humor.

title: Jimi Hendrix
description: The 2004 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial features Jimi Hendrix performing a dynamic rendition of "Purple Haze."  The ad is primarily a performance piece, showcasing Hendrix's energetic stage presence and musical talent.  Quick cuts between the performance and Pepsi products are interspersed, subtly associating the brand with the iconic musician's powerful energy and legacy. The overall tone is celebratory and vibrant, connecting Pepsi with a feeling of cool and excitement.

title: Perfect Match
description: The 2004 Monster.com Super Bowl commercial, "Perfect Match," showcases various individuals from diverse backgrounds using Monster.com to find jobs.  The ad emphasizes the wide range of employment opportunities available through the platform. It features quick cuts of people in various professions—a chef, an office worker, a construction worker—all finding success after using Monster.com. The overall tone is upbeat and optimistic, highlighting the power of the website to connect people with their ideal jobs.

title: Dryer Sheet
description: The 2004 McDonald's Super Bowl commercial features a man using a dryer sheet to clean a variety of messes, including spilled soda and a dirty car.  He then uses it to clean a greasy burger, implying the sheet somehow cleans the burger, which is then magically transformed into a pristine, appealing McDonald's burger. The ad ends with a voiceover stating that the McDonald's burger is "so good, it's worth cleaning up for."

title: Homer Simpson
description: The 2004 Mastercard Super Bowl ad features Homer Simpson attempting to purchase a luxurious item (possibly a car) with his Mastercard.  He's initially denied due to insufficient funds, leading to humorous reactions and a montage of everyday purchases, highlighting the many transactions possible with a Mastercard.  The ad concludes with him successfully making a smaller purchase, showcasing the card's everyday usability.

title: Teeth
description: The 2004 Lay's "Teeth" Super Bowl commercial features a man intensely focused on eating a Lay's potato chip.  As he savors the chip, his teeth mysteriously begin to grow longer and longer, culminating in a comically exaggerated and absurd length.  The ad emphasizes the satisfying crunch and flavor of the chip, using the exaggerated reaction to highlight the enjoyment.

title: In What Gear
description: The 2004 Ford GT Super Bowl commercial showcases the car's speed and power through dynamic driving shots.  The advertisement emphasizes the car's performance capabilities, primarily focusing on its exhilarating acceleration and handling.  The visuals are fast-paced and energetic, highlighting the sleek design of the Ford GT against various scenic backdrops. Minimal dialogue is used, relying instead on the visual spectacle of the car in action. The overall tone is exciting and aspirational, targeting a high-performance automotive audience.

title: Fergus
description: The 2004 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Fergus," features a Clydesdale horse named Fergus who escapes from a Budweiser Clydesdale stable.  He makes his way through a bustling city, causing minor chaos before eventually finding his way back to the stable and back to his fellow horses. The ad uses humor and heartwarming elements showing Fergus' journey.

title: Frank
description: The 2004 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial "Frank" features a man named Frank who's incredibly unlucky.  Various mishaps befall him, culminating in him accidentally destroying a Bud Light display.  Despite his string of misfortunes, he maintains a positive attitude and even manages a small victory at the end, subtly showcasing the resilience associated with enjoying a Bud Light.  The humor lies in the absurdity of Frank's misfortunes, creating a lighthearted and relatable narrative.

title: Donkey Clydesdale
description: A lonely donkey on a farm befriends a Budweiser Clydesdale horse.  The unlikely pair engages in playful antics, culminating in a heartwarming scene where the donkey attempts to participate in the Clydesdales' iconic hitch. The ad emphasizes friendship and showcases the Clydesdales' gentle nature, concluding with a Budweiser logo and tagline. The focus is on the visual humor and emotional connection between the two animals.

title: Sleigh Ride
description: The 2004 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Sleigh Ride," features a group of friends enjoying a snowy, wintery scene.  They're playfully interacting, drinking Bud Light, and having a good time. The overall tone is lighthearted and jovial, emphasizing the fun and camaraderie associated with sharing Bud Light with friends during the holidays. The ad utilizes a playful, slightly absurd scenario without a specific narrative arc, focusing instead on evoking a feeling of festive enjoyment.

title: Top Speed
description: The 2004 AOL "Top Speed" Super Bowl commercial showcases a futuristic, sleek car speeding through various environments.  The car's speed is emphasized, correlating with the speed of AOL's dial-up internet connection.  The ad features quick cuts and dynamic visuals, culminating in the AOL logo and tagline, highlighting the fast internet service.

title: Slam Dunk
description: The 2004 7UP Super Bowl commercial, "Slam Dunk," features a series of increasingly absurd and comical scenarios where people's attempts at simple actions are hilariously disrupted by unexpected events.  A man trying to dunk a basketball is continually thwarted, a woman's attempt to delicately place a flower is interrupted, and a man attempting to light a cigarette is repeatedly failed. The humor derives from the escalating chaos and the unexpected twists, all while maintaining a lighthearted and energetic tone.  The ad ends with the 7UP logo.

title: Bears Find Food
description: The 2004 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial, "Bears Find Food," features a group of polar bears navigating a treacherous, snowy landscape.  Their journey is fueled by an unwavering desire for Pepsi.  The bears encounter various obstacles, showcasing their resourcefulness and determination.  The humor lies in the unexpected juxtaposition of the bears' arctic environment and their craving for a refreshing Pepsi, culminating in a satisfying and comical moment of refreshment.

title: Astronaut
description: The 2003 Sony Astronaut Super Bowl commercial depicts a lone astronaut, seemingly stranded on a desolate planet, using a Sony Walkman to listen to music.  The visuals are stark and minimalist, focusing on the astronaut's isolation and the small comfort provided by the music. The ad emphasizes the portability and enduring appeal of Sony's audio technology, even in extreme circumstances.  The commercial ends with the Sony logo and tagline.

title: Yoga
description: The 2003 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial features a series of comedic vignettes.  A man attempts to perform yoga poses, but repeatedly fails hilariously, culminating in a crash.  The humor comes from the unexpected and exaggerated physical reactions of the man struggling with yoga, and the contrast between the serene nature of yoga and his clumsy attempts. The ad ends with the Bud Light logo and a tagline.

title: Presidents
description: The 2003 Mastercard Super Bowl commercial, "Presidents," features a series of historical US presidents (played by actors) using Mastercard to make everyday purchases.  The humorous juxtaposition of these figures with mundane transactions, such as buying groceries or gas, highlights the accessibility and widespread use of Mastercard. The ad concludes with the Mastercard tagline and logo.

title: Twins Remote
description: Two identical twins use a remote control to swap places with each other, creating humorous situations. One twin is enjoying a relaxing day at home while the other is at a busy, chaotic office.  The remote allows them to instantly switch places, highlighting the refreshing aspects of Coors beer. The ad culminates with both twins enjoying a Coors Light, emphasizing relaxation and refreshment.

title: Third Arm
description: The 2003 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Third Arm," features a man with a third arm inexplicably sprouting from his stomach.  This extra limb hilariously interferes with his daily life, causing chaos in various scenarios, such as trying to eat, play pool, and even driving. The humor arises from the absurdity of the situation and the man's continued attempts to cope with his unusual appendage. The ad concludes with him effortlessly opening a Bud Light with his third arm, highlighting the ease and convenience of the product.

title: Rainbow Connection
description: The 2003 HotJobs Super Bowl commercial, "Rainbow Connection," uses a whimsical, almost surreal approach. It features a diverse group of people, seemingly from different walks of life, interconnected through a vibrant, rainbow-like string.  The string stretches across various settings, symbolically connecting job seekers with opportunities. The overall tone is optimistic and playful, emphasizing the broad reach and effectiveness of HotJobs in connecting talent with employers.

title: Crazy with Don Cheadle
description: The 2003 NFL Super Bowl commercial features Don Cheadle portraying various scenarios of football fans going crazy over the game, highlighting the excitement and passion surrounding NFL football.  The ad uses quick cuts and comedic exaggeration to show fans' reactions—from extreme celebrations to outlandish behaviors—all while emphasizing the unpredictable and thrilling nature of NFL games.  Cheadle acts as a narrator, adding humor to the chaotic scenes.

title: Gilligan’s Island
description: The 2003 MLIFE Super Bowl commercial reimagines the Gilligan's Island theme song and cast.  It features the familiar characters on the island, playfully interacting in various scenarios.  The ad uses humor and nostalgia to connect with viewers. While the island setting is maintained, the commercial emphasizes the MLIFE brand, showcasing it subtly through the characters' interactions. The overall tone is lighthearted and comedic, aiming to establish a memorable association between the brand and the beloved television show.

title: Tiki and Ronde Barber
original_title: 2003 VISA CHECK CARD – Tiki and Ronde Barber
description: The 2003 Visa Check Card commercial features twin brothers Tiki and Ronde Barber, NFL players.  The ad opens with Tiki and Ronde playfully arguing over who should pay for a meal with their Visa check cards.  The scene shifts to highlight the convenience and acceptance of Visa cards at various locations. The focus is on the ease and speed of using the card for transactions.  The brothers' friendly rivalry continues throughout, emphasizing the straightforward and practical use of the Visa check card.

title: Roommate
description: A Budweiser commercial depicting a friendly competition between two roommates over a Budweiser. One roommate, dressed in a suit, tries to subtly outmaneuver the other to grab the last Budweiser. The comedic timing and playful actions highlight the shared enjoyment of the beer. The ad ends with both roommates happily sharing the beer, emphasizing camaraderie and shared experiences.

title: 5th Dentist
