description: The Trident "5th Dentist" Super Bowl commercial from 2003 features a series of dentists discussing Trident chewing gum.  Four dentists enthusiastically endorse the gum's sugar-free properties and fresh breath benefits.  A fifth dentist, however, hesitantly expresses a less positive opinion, creating a humorous contrast and memorable tagline. The ad relies on the unexpected dissenting opinion to build intrigue and comedic effect.  The focus is on the refreshing qualities and health benefits of the gum.

title: Hydrant
description: The 2003 Sierra Mist Super Bowl commercial, titled "Hydrant," features a group of thirsty individuals desperately seeking refreshment.  A fire hydrant magically transforms into a giant Sierra Mist soda dispenser, satisfying their thirst with a massive gush of the lemon-lime soda. The ad highlights the refreshing quality of the drink in a fantastical, humorous way. The visuals are bright and energetic, emphasizing the fun and playful nature of the brand.

title: Willie Nelson
description: The 2003 H&R Block Super Bowl commercial features Willie Nelson strumming his guitar in a relaxed setting.  He sings a slightly altered version of a song, emphasizing the ease and simplicity of using H&R Block for tax preparation. The ad uses a calm, folksy tone and focuses on the trustworthiness associated with the brand, contrasting with the potential stress of tax season.  There's no significant plot or action; it's primarily a feel-good, celebrity-endorsed message.

title: Heimlich
description: The 2003 Dodge Ram Super Bowl commercial, titled "Heimlich," features a dramatic scene where a man performs the Heimlich maneuver on a choking woman in a restaurant.  The rescue is unexpectedly interrupted by the arrival of a powerful Dodge Ram truck, pulling up with a flourish.  The truck's arrival seems to resolve the tension, implying its strength and capability can overcome any obstacle. The ad emphasizes the truck's ruggedness and power indirectly through this unusual narrative.

title: Strongman
description: The 2003 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Strongman," features a comedic strongman effortlessly lifting incredibly heavy objects, such as a car and a house, with Bud Light cans seemingly adding to his strength.  The humor lies in the absurdity of his feats and the implication that Bud Light enhances his superhuman abilities. The ad concludes with him lifting a giant Bud Light can, emphasizing the brand's association with strength and fun.

title: Osbornes
description: The 2003 Pepsi Twist commercial, titled "Osbornes," features a family, the Osbornes, engaging in various humorous everyday activities.  The situations are slightly exaggerated, showcasing quirky family dynamics and playful interactions.  The Pepsi Twist product is subtly integrated into the scenes, primarily through visual presence, not explicitly highlighting specific features or benefits.  The overall tone is lighthearted and comedic, emphasizing the enjoyment of family time.

title: Rough Day
description: The 2003 McDonald's Super Bowl commercial, "Rough Day," depicts a series of unfortunate events happening to a man throughout his day.  He experiences car trouble, a dropped briefcase, a spilled drink, and a missed bus.  At the end, he finds solace and a happy ending at a McDonald's restaurant, suggesting that even on a rough day, McDonald's offers comfort and satisfaction.

title: Great Listener
description: The 2003 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "Great Listener," showcases a Clydesdale horse patiently listening to a frog's concerns.  The frog, perched on the horse's shoulder, expresses anxieties about upcoming challenges.  The horse displays empathy and understanding, highlighting Budweiser's association with companionship and shared experiences. The ad concludes with the Budweiser logo and tagline.

title: Instant Replay
description: The 2003 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "Instant Replay," uses humorous slow-motion to showcase a Clydesdale horse's athletic abilities.  The ad opens with a close-up on a Budweiser bottle, then transitions to a Clydesdale elegantly leaping over hurdles, showcasing its strength and grace.  The slow-motion shots highlight the horse's movement, emphasizing its elegance and power.  The commercial concludes with the Budweiser logo and slogan.

title: Celine Dion
description: The 2003 Chrysler Crossfire Super Bowl commercial features Celine Dion singing a dramatic rendition of Bob Dylan's 'A Hard Rain's A-Gonna Fall'.  The visuals intercut shots of the sleek, new Crossfire roadster driving through various landscapes with close-ups of Dion's emotive performance. The ad evokes a feeling of power, sophistication, and a sense of yearning, associating the car with a heightened emotional experience.  The car is presented as a symbol of freedom and personal expression.

title: Yao Ming
description: The 2003 Visa commercial features Yao Ming, then a rising NBA star, using his Visa card for various purchases.  The ad showcases the convenience and acceptance of Visa cards in everyday situations, from buying groceries to paying for a taxi.  The scenes are quick cuts showing a variety of locations and transactions, highlighting the global reach of Visa. Yao Ming's presence provides a memorable and positive association with the brand.

title: Upside Down Clown
description: The 2003 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Upside Down Clown," features a series of surreal and humorous scenarios.  A clown is shown upside down, inexplicably, in various locations.  The situations are absurd and unexpected, culminating in the clown being launched into the air.  The ad relies heavily on visual gags and unexpected juxtapositions rather than a narrative storyline.  The Bud Light logo is prominently displayed throughout, associating the brand with the quirky humor.

title: No Pets Allowed
description: The 2003 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "No Pets Allowed," features a man sneaking his dog into a bar.  The dog, dressed in a tiny suit, causes a ruckus, culminating in a playful bar fight involving patrons and the dog.  The commercial uses slapstick humor and showcases the Bud Light brand in a casual, fun bar setting.  The focus is on the humorous antics of the dog and the lighthearted reaction of those around him. The ad ends with the dog and his owner enjoying a Bud Light.

title: Mother In Law
description: A man is relaxing on his couch when his mother-in-law unexpectedly arrives for a visit.  He attempts to subtly hide his stash of Bud Light beer, but she quickly discovers it.  The situation escalates into a humorous exchange where she ultimately joins him in enjoying a beer, revealing a surprisingly easy-going and jovial relationship.  The ad concludes with both enjoying the beer together.

title: Hermit Crab
description: The 2003 Bud Light "Hermit Crab" Super Bowl commercial features a man who is frustrated because his friends have left him to watch the Super Bowl alone. He's shown despondently trying to make a crab shell fit over his head and drinking a Bud Light.  The commercial then cuts to a shot of a giant crab shell, implying a solution to his loneliness. The humor lies in the absurdity of the situation and the man's desperate attempt to fit in.

title: Go Tagless with Jackie Chan, Michael Jordan
original_title: 2003 HANES – Go Tagless with Jackie Chan, Michael Jordan
description: The 2003 Hanes commercial features Jackie Chan and Michael Jordan playfully demonstrating the comfort and tagless design of Hanes underwear.  The ad opens with Chan and Jordan in a playful sparring match, highlighting the lack of irritating tags.  It emphasizes the comfort and freedom of movement provided by the tagless underwear. The humorous interaction between the two celebrities drives home the message of superior comfort.

title: Michael Jordan
description: The 2003 Gatorade commercial features Michael Jordan relentlessly training.  The ad showcases Jordan's intense workout regimen, highlighting his dedication and perseverance.  Quick cuts show him pushing his physical limits through various drills and exercises.  The overall message emphasizes the connection between hard work, athletic performance, and Gatorade's role in fueling athletes. The visuals are fast-paced and energetic, focusing on Jordan's determination and the physical demands of his training.

title: Castaway
description: A FedEx package containing a volleyball, reminiscent of the movie Cast Away, washes ashore on a deserted island.  A lone figure, seemingly the package's recipient, is shown living a primitive life. The FedEx package arrives, providing him with much-needed supplies, a lifeline enabling him to signal for rescue and escape his isolated existence.  The ad emphasizes FedEx's reliability and ability to reach even the most remote locations.

title: Monkey Takes Dip
description: A monkey, dressed in a tiny tuxedo, sits by a pool.  He's clearly unhappy with the offered drink (presumably soda). A Sierra Mist bottle is then presented. The monkey happily accepts the Sierra Mist and takes a refreshing dip in the pool.  The ad emphasizes the drink's refreshing qualities through the monkey's actions and setting.

title: Driverless Truck
description: The 2003 Monster.com Super Bowl commercial depicts a futuristic, driverless truck autonomously navigating a highway.  The truck is shown hauling various Monster.com-branded cargo, emphasizing the company's ability to connect employers and job seekers. The ad's humor comes from the unexpected and slightly absurd nature of a driverless truck successfully performing its job, highlighting the ease and efficiency of finding work through Monster.com.

title: Stampede
description: The Levi's 2003 Super Bowl commercial, "Stampede," depicts a diverse group of individuals – cowboys, Native Americans, city dwellers, and others – all converging on a central location.  They're initially shown in their separate environments, but a powerful, unifying force (possibly the music and atmosphere) brings them together in a celebratory dance.  The ad showcases Levi's clothing worn by the participants, emphasizing its versatility and appeal to a broad demographic.

title: Terry Tate Office Linebacker
description: Terry Tate, a linebacker, is hired by an office to boost employee productivity.  He uses aggressive football tactics to motivate and 'tackle' underperforming employees, causing comical chaos and destruction in the office. The ad showcases his brutal but effective methods, culminating in a celebratory scene with his boss. The Reebok logo is prominently displayed throughout, associating the brand with powerful and determined individuals.

title: Dolphin
description: The 2002 Yahoo! Super Bowl commercial features a dolphin leaping out of the ocean and gracefully soaring through the air, seemingly defying gravity.  It lands on a beach, then swims back into the sea.  The Yahoo! logo appears, implying the unexpected and playful nature of the internet experience. The ad is short, surreal, and memorable, lacking any dialogue or human interaction.

title: Tushy
description: The 2002 Budweiser "Tushy" Super Bowl commercial features a Clydesdale horse relieving itself on a competitor's beer truck.  The humor derives from the unexpected and slightly crude act, contrasted with the typically majestic imagery associated with Budweiser's Clydesdale horses.  The spot ends with the Budweiser logo and tagline, implying the superior quality of their beer.

title: I wanna vacation
description: The 2002 Universal Orlando Super Bowl commercial features a montage of people expressing their desire for a vacation, interspersed with shots of Universal Orlando Resort attractions and amenities.  It emphasizes the excitement and fun of a Universal Orlando vacation, showcasing various rides, shows, and the overall atmosphere.  The ad uses upbeat music and quick cuts to create a sense of energy and excitement, ultimately aiming to entice viewers to visit the resort.

title: Stenographer
description: The 2002 Hotjobs.com Super Bowl commercial features a fast-paced montage of diverse professionals in various workplaces.  It emphasizes the variety of job opportunities available through the website.  The ad uses quick cuts, energetic music, and a rapid-fire delivery to highlight the speed and efficiency of finding a job with Hotjobs.com.  The overall tone is upbeat and optimistic, focusing on the potential for career advancement.

title: Ready for Meeting
description: The 2002 Computer Associates Super Bowl commercial depicts a business meeting where executives are frustrated by outdated technology and inefficient processes.  The scene transitions to show a sleek, modern office using CA's technology, symbolizing increased efficiency and collaboration. The ad emphasizes the benefits of CA's software solutions by contrasting the chaotic old system with the smooth, organized new one.  The overall message is that CA helps businesses improve productivity and streamline operations.

title: Anniversary Card
description: The 2002 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "Anniversary Card," depicts a heartwarming story of a long-married couple reminiscing over their life together.  The ad utilizes a series of flashbacks triggered by looking at an anniversary card, showcasing moments from their courtship, marriage, and raising a family. The commercial emphasizes the couple's enduring love and connection, subtly associating Budweiser with these positive memories and feelings of companionship.

title: Tax Reform
description: The 2002 H&R Block Super Bowl commercial depicts a variety of everyday people in various scenarios experiencing frustration with complex tax forms.  It emphasizes the difficulty of navigating tax laws.  The ad then transitions to show H&R Block representatives assisting these individuals, ultimately highlighting the ease and simplicity offered by using H&R Block's services to resolve tax concerns.  The overall tone suggests relief and problem-solving.

title: 7 Degrees with Kevin Bacon
original_title: 2002 VISA CHECK CARD – 7 Degrees with Kevin Bacon
description: The 2002 Visa Check Card Super Bowl commercial features Kevin Bacon explaining the "six degrees of separation" concept, playfully connecting him to various seemingly unrelated people through Visa transactions.  The ad emphasizes the widespread use of Visa cards, showcasing diverse individuals using them for everyday purchases.  It's a lighthearted and humorous approach to demonstrating the reach and acceptance of the Visa Check Card.

title: Falcon
description: The 2002 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, titled "Falcon," features a man attempting to impress a woman by showcasing his falconry skills.  The humorous ad shows the man's attempts to control his falcon backfiring repeatedly, culminating in the bird causing chaos and ultimately landing on the woman's head.  The commercial emphasizes the lighthearted and comical aspects of unexpected situations, concluding with a Bud Light logo and tagline.

title: Cedric Advice
description: The 2002 Bud Light commercial features comedian Cedric the Entertainer offering humorous relationship advice to a man contemplating a romantic gesture.  Cedric's advice, delivered with his signature comedic timing and charm, centers around the importance of having cold Bud Light readily available for a successful romantic encounter. The ad uses a simple, straightforward scenario to highlight the brand's association with fun and social situations.

title: Monkey Musical
description: The 2002 ETRADE Super Bowl commercial, "Monkey Musical," features a group of monkeys dressed in formal attire performing a sophisticated musical number.  They play various instruments with surprising skill and precision, culminating in a final flourish. The ad uses humor and unexpected visuals to highlight the brand, suggesting its ease of use and sophisticated capabilities in a memorable and lighthearted way.  The monkeys themselves become a memorable visual representation of ETRADE.

title: Pee Wee Football
description: The 2002 McDonald's Super Bowl commercial features a pee-wee football game where the players exhibit exaggerated, comedically clumsy actions.  The focus is on the kids' enthusiasm and the fun of the game, with McDonald's subtly integrated into the background.  The ad highlights the energy and excitement of youth sports, ultimately associating McDonald's with positive family experiences.

title: on FOX
description: The 2002 NASCAR Super Bowl commercial showcases thrilling on-track racing action from the NASCAR season.  The ad features fast-paced cuts of close racing, crashes, and celebratory moments.  It emphasizes the excitement and intensity of NASCAR, using mostly footage from races, interspersed with the FOX logo.  The overall tone is energetic and action-packed, designed to promote the upcoming NASCAR season on FOX.

title: Satin Sheets
description: The 2002 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Satin Sheets," features a man waking up in a luxurious hotel room, seemingly after a night of partying.  He's disoriented and confused, eventually discovering his surroundings and the source of his confusion: he's surrounded by satin sheets, a playful exaggeration of the feeling of relaxation and comfort associated with Bud Light. The ad uses humor to associate the beer with a luxurious, albeit slightly absurd, experience.

title: Barry Bonds, Hank Aaron
description: The Schwab commercial features baseball legends Barry Bonds and Hank Aaron discussing their investment strategies.  Bonds, known for his power hitting, emphasizes the importance of aggressive investing, while Aaron, known for his consistency, advocates a more conservative approach.  The ad uses their contrasting styles to illustrate the diverse investment options available through Schwab, highlighting the importance of personalized financial planning to meet individual goals and risk tolerance.  The commercial concludes with a call to action to contact Schwab for financial advice.

title: Focus Group
description: The 2002 Quiznos Super Bowl commercial, titled "Focus Group," uses a mock focus group setting to showcase their toasted subs.  Participants initially express skepticism, but after tasting the sub, their reactions shift dramatically, from polite indifference to enthusiastic approval.  Their exaggerated, over-the-top expressions highlight the deliciousness of the sandwich and the satisfying crunch of the toasted bread. The ad concludes with the Quiznos logo and tagline.

title: Generations with Britney Spears
description: The Pepsi Generations ad features Britney Spears across different decades, showcasing iconic Pepsi imagery and moments from the past.  It starts with a black and white scene reminiscent of the 1950s, progresses through the 60s and 70s, and culminates in a modern, colorful setting with Britney.  The ad emphasizes Pepsi's long-standing presence throughout American pop culture, using nostalgia and a celebrity endorsement to connect with viewers.

title: Little Black Dress
description: The 2002 Dockers Super Bowl commercial, "Little Black Dress," features a man agonizing over his wardrobe choices for a date.  He tries on various outfits, culminating in a stylish Dockers suit.  The ad emphasizes the versatility and sophistication of Dockers clothing, contrasting it with the chaos of choosing less suitable attire.  The humor lies in the relatable struggle of choosing the perfect outfit, ultimately suggesting Dockers provides the confident solution.

title: How ya Doin’
description: The 2002 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "How ya Doin'," features a Clydesdale horse playfully interacting with a group of frogs.  The frogs, initially wary, eventually join the horse in a friendly, comical exchange. The ad emphasizes the Budweiser brand alongside the heartwarming interaction between the unlikely friends.  The scene is idyllic and pastoral, ending with the Budweiser logo and tagline.  The commercial relies on visual humor and cute animal interactions.

title: Ground Zero Clydesdales Bow
description: The 2002 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial shows a lone Clydesdale horse walking through the devastated streets of lower Manhattan following the 9/11 attacks.  The horse pauses at Ground Zero, then bows its head in a moment of somber reflection. The ad features no dialogue, relying solely on imagery and music to convey a message of remembrance and resilience.

title: Sam Adams
description: The 2002 Sam Adams Super Bowl commercial for United Way depicts a diverse group of people from various walks of life enjoying a Sam Adams beer together.  The ad emphasizes community and togetherness, subtly highlighting the brand's association with charitable giving. It features a montage of everyday scenes, showing people interacting positively and enjoying their leisure time.  There's no overt call to action for the beer itself, rather the focus is on the feeling of community and connection, indirectly promoting the United Way organization.

title: Rudy Giuliani
description: The 2002 Monster.com Super Bowl ad features former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani discussing his experience with job searching.  He emphasizes the importance of finding the right job and how Monster.com can help. The ad uses a serious, straightforward tone, focusing on Giuliani's credibility and Monster.com's ability to connect job seekers with opportunities. Giuliani speaks directly to the camera, highlighting the site's ease of use and effectiveness. The ad features minimal visuals beyond Giuliani himself.

title: Fit Guy
description: The 2002 Monster.com Super Bowl commercial, "Fit Guy," features a man obsessively exercising and meticulously preparing his resume, highlighting his dedication to finding the perfect job.  He performs various fitness routines, showcasing his commitment to health and self-improvement.  The ad concludes with him confidently submitting his resume online via Monster.com, emphasizing the site's ease of use and the potential for finding a perfect career match. The overall tone is humorous, particularly the contrast between his intense fitness regimen and the mundane act of job hunting.

title: Danny Devito
description: The 2002 Lipton Brisk commercial features Danny DeVito as a disgruntled office worker who is incredibly thirsty.  He's shown enduring a variety of frustrating office situations before finally grabbing a cold Lipton Brisk iced tea.  The relief and satisfaction he experiences after taking a sip is highlighted, emphasizing the drink's refreshing qualities. The ad uses humor to portray the daily struggles of office life and positions Brisk as the ultimate solution for thirst and frustration.

title: Parking Spot
description: The 2002 Cadillac Super Bowl commercial, "Parking Spot," showcases a man's determined pursuit of a coveted parking space.  He skillfully navigates a crowded parking lot, showcasing his driving prowess and the Cadillac's maneuverability. The ad culminates in him triumphantly parking, highlighting the car's features subtly through the action. The overall tone is lighthearted and emphasizes the driving experience.

title: RoboBash
description: The 2002 Bud Light RoboBash Super Bowl commercial features a futuristic robot-themed party.  Robots, some resembling popular movie robots, engage in a chaotic, humorous fight with various objects like pool cues and oversized boxing gloves.  The overall tone is lighthearted and silly, showcasing Bud Light's association with fun and good times.  The ad ends with a group of people enjoying Bud Light at the party. The robots themselves are the primary focus, rather than any human characters.

title: Crazy Legs
description: The Levi's "Crazy Legs" Super Bowl ad from 2002 features a diverse group of people showcasing their unique dance moves and styles while wearing Levi's jeans.  The commercial emphasizes individuality and self-expression through energetic choreography set to upbeat music.  Different locations and dance styles are shown, creating a vibrant and fun atmosphere.  The focus is on the versatility and style of Levi's jeans, showcasing them as a part of various personalities and lifestyles.

title: Subway Miracle
description: The 2001 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial, "Subway Miracle," depicts a seemingly ordinary subway ride transforming into an extraordinary experience.  A young man, bored on the train, suddenly finds himself surrounded by dancers and musicians performing a vibrant, energetic routine.  The mood shifts dramatically as the subway car bursts with color and excitement, culminating in a joyous celebration. Pepsi is prominently featured throughout, emphasizing its association with fun and unexpected moments.

title: Big Springs
description: The FedEx "Big Springs" Super Bowl ad from 2001 depicts a dramatic, almost cinematic chase scene.  A FedEx delivery truck, racing against time, navigates a challenging mountain road, showcasing its durability and reliability in a harsh environment. The driver skillfully maneuvers the truck, highlighting FedEx's commitment to timely delivery, even under pressure. The ad ends with the package successfully delivered, emphasizing the company's dependability.

title: Chat Without Talking
description: The 2001 Verizon Super Bowl commercial showcases the then-new technology of text messaging.  It depicts various scenarios of people using the service: a couple flirting, a friend offering support, and colleagues coordinating a meeting.  The ad emphasizes the convenience and efficiency of communicating without speaking, highlighting the immediacy and informal nature of text messaging compared to traditional phone calls.  The overall tone is upbeat and positive, showcasing the revolutionary aspect of this new communication method.

title: Auction
description: The 2001 Mastercard Super Bowl commercial, titled "Auction," depicts a humorous bidding war between two men at an auction.  One man persistently outbids the other for seemingly mundane items, culminating in a priceless, antique vase.  The final scene reveals the losing bidder's Mastercard, highlighting the ease and acceptance of the card even in high-stakes situations.  The humor lies in the escalating absurdity of the bidding and the unexpected reveal.

title: Pet Store
description: The 2001 Visa Check Card commercial depicts a lighthearted scene in a pet store. A man is buying various pet supplies, showcasing the ease and convenience of using a Visa Check Card for everyday purchases.  The ad emphasizes the practicality and acceptance of the card, highlighting its use in a common retail setting. The focus is on the simple transaction and the implied convenience for the consumer.

title: Otto
description: The 2001 Bud Light commercial "Otto" features a clumsy, yet lovable, Clydesdale horse named Otto.  He's shown struggling with various tasks around the Budweiser brewery, causing comical mishaps.  The humor lies in Otto's clumsiness contrasted with the serious work environment.  The ad ends with Otto successfully delivering a Bud Light, showcasing the brand's lighthearted personality.

title: Transplant
description: The Levi's 2001 Super Bowl commercial, "Transplant," depicts a young man moving from a small, rural town to a bustling city.  He's seen packing his belongings, including a pair of Levi's 501 jeans.  The ad showcases the transition and contrasts the different environments, emphasizing the adaptability and enduring nature of Levi's jeans. It features a montage of images representing both the old and new environments, concluding with the man in the city wearing his jeans.

title: Wake Up Call
description: The 2001 Computer Associates Super Bowl commercial, "Wake Up Call," depicts a chaotic office scene where employees are struggling with inefficient systems.  A stressed executive is shown frantically trying to manage various tasks before collapsing.  The ad then transitions to a montage showcasing Computer Associates' software solutions, emphasizing improved efficiency and productivity.  The commercial concludes with the CA logo and tagline, highlighting the benefits of their technology for streamlining business operations.

title: Perfect Day
description: The 2001 NFL Super Bowl commercial, "Perfect Day," depicts a montage of idyllic scenes showcasing various aspects of everyday life, interweaving them with NFL football game highlights.  It features families, friends, and children enjoying recreational activities interspersed with thrilling plays and the excitement of NFL games. The overall message suggests that football is a part of the fabric of American life, adding joy and shared experiences to everyday moments.

title: Selfie
description: A Volkswagen Passat driver takes a series of increasingly absurd selfies with various people and objects, culminating in a humorous, chaotic montage. The driver's actions cause escalating reactions from onlookers in comical ways, such as a dog reacting hilariously to being included in a selfie. The ad emphasizes the fun and spontaneous nature of owning a Volkswagen, rather than focusing on specific car features.

title: Tree
description: The Volkswagen 'Tree' Super Bowl commercial from 2001 features a young boy who plants a small tree sapling.  Years pass in a sped-up time-lapse, showcasing the tree's growth alongside the boy's life and a Volkswagen Beetle's changing models. The ad culminates with the now-grown tree providing shade for the adult man and his own family, underlining the lasting quality and generational appeal of the Volkswagen.

title: Late For Wedding
description: A Volkswagen Beetle driver, rushing to a wedding, encounters various humorous obstacles: a runaway dog, a flat tire, and a flooded road.  Despite these setbacks, the driver maintains a calm demeanor, showcasing the car's resilience. The ad concludes with the driver arriving fashionably late but successfully making it to the wedding, suggesting the car's reliability even under stressful circumstances. The overall tone is lighthearted and focuses on problem-solving with a touch of quirky charm.

title: Catch Phrase Crunch
description: The 2001 Snickers Crunchers Super Bowl commercial, "Catch Phrase Crunch," features a series of people misusing popular catchphrases in everyday situations.  A man says "Hasta la vista, baby" while leaving a party, a woman exclaims "Show me the money!" when ordering coffee, and another says "You had me at hello" in a mundane office setting.  The absurdity of the situations highlights the unexpected and enjoyable crunch of the new Snickers Crunchers candy bar, which is shown at the end as a solution to the catchphrase chaos. The ad uses humor to showcase the product.

title: Roller Coaster
description: The 2001 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial, "Roller Coaster," features a thrilling roller coaster ride with unexpected twists.  A group of diverse individuals enjoys the ride, experiencing moments of exhilaration and fear.  The Pepsi logo is prominently displayed throughout, associating the brand with the excitement and shared experience.  The ad culminates with everyone laughing and enjoying the ride, emphasizing the fun and refreshment that Pepsi brings.

title: Kasparov vs Pepsi Machine
description: The 2001 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial features chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov playing a chess match against a Pepsi vending machine.  The machine, seemingly powered by Pepsi, makes surprisingly strategic moves, ultimately outsmarting Kasparov.  The ad uses humor and a bit of surprise to highlight Pepsi's unexpected and refreshing qualities, contrasting Kasparov's intense focus with the vending machine's playful intelligence.

title: Bob Dole
description: The 2001 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial features Bob Dole, the former Senate Majority Leader, participating in a Pepsi taste test challenge against younger individuals.  The ad uses humor as Dole, despite his age, easily wins the challenge, showcasing Pepsi's refreshing taste. The commercial emphasizes a lighthearted, relatable contrast between generations while promoting the drink.

title: Running With Squirrels
description: The 2001 EDS Super Bowl commercial, "Running With Squirrels," depicts a chaotic office scene where employees are overwhelmed and inefficient.  A man runs through the office, literally running with squirrels, symbolizing the disorganization.  The ad then transitions to show how EDS's technology solutions streamline processes and create a more efficient and organized workplace, contrasting the initial chaos with a calm, productive environment.  The commercial emphasizes the benefits of EDS's services for improving business operations.

title: Security Guard
description: The ETRADE Super Bowl 2001 commercial features a security guard diligently protecting a server room.  He meticulously checks for intruders, even inspecting a suspicious-looking chimpanzee. The humor lies in the contrast between the guard's intense security measures and the seemingly mundane task of protecting the server.  The ad concludes with a shot of the E*TRADE logo, subtly implying the security and reliability of their online brokerage services.

title: Dot Com Ghost Town
description: The E*TRADE 2001 Super Bowl commercial, "Dot Com Ghost Town," depicts a deserted office building, once a bustling dot-com company, now eerily empty.  A lone cowboy rides through the desolate space on horseback, symbolizing the bursting of the dot-com bubble. He eventually finds an employee still working, highlighting E*TRADE's resilience and stability in contrast to the failing dot-coms.

title: Ali Landry
description: The 2001 Doritos Super Bowl commercial features Ali Landry, a beautiful woman, enjoying a bag of Doritos.  She playfully interacts with the camera, showcasing the chips and her enjoyment. The ad is simple, focusing on her charm and the product itself with minimal dialogue or plot. It emphasizes the deliciousness of Doritos in a light-hearted, flirtatious manner, relying on Landry's attractiveness as a main selling point. The commercial ends with her smiling and offering a final look at the product.

title: Hudson Riverdance
description: The 2001 Diet Dr Pepper Super Bowl commercial, "Hudson Riverdance," features a tap-dancing troupe performing an elaborate routine on the Hudson River.  The dancers, in coordinated outfits, move rhythmically and energetically across the water's surface, seemingly defying gravity. The ad is fast-paced and visually striking, with a focus on the impressive dance choreography.  The only branding is the Diet Dr Pepper logo at the end. The overall tone is upbeat and playful.

title: N’SYNC
description: The 2001 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial features N'SYNC performing their hit song "Bye Bye Bye" in a lively, energetic setting.  The band interacts with various people and settings, including a bar and a celebratory atmosphere. The focus is primarily on the band's performance and the association of Budweiser with youthful energy and fun.  The ad utilizes quick cuts and dynamic visuals, keeping the pace fast and engaging throughout.

title: What Are You Doing?
description: The 2001 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "What Are You Doing?", features a Clydesdale horse escaping from its Budweiser stable and embarking on a joyful romp through a city.  It interacts playfully with people and other animals, showcasing its gentle nature. The horse's escapade culminates with its return to the stable, implying freedom and a connection to nature. The ad uses minimal dialogue and relies on heartwarming visuals to convey its message.

title: Working Late
description: The Bud Light commercial, "Working Late," depicts a man working late at the office.  He's visibly tired and frustrated. He then pours himself a Bud Light. The scene shifts, and he's suddenly playing basketball with colleagues and having a fun time. The implication is that Bud Light helps him unwind and enjoy his time after work.  The ad focuses on relaxation and camaraderie, contrasting the stress of work with the enjoyment of a Bud Light.

title: Cedric The Entertainer
description: Cedric the Entertainer stars in this 2001 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial.  The ad features a series of vignettes showing people enjoying Bud Light in various social settings.  Cedric acts as a sort of narrator, interjecting comedic commentary on the scenes. The overall tone is lighthearted and humorous, showcasing the beer as a drink enjoyed by friends in casual settings.  The commercial relies heavily on Cedric's comedic timing and personality to sell the product.

title: Marble
description: The 2001 HotJobs.com Super Bowl commercial, titled "Marble," features a man meticulously rolling a marble across various obstacles in a minimalist setting.  The marble's journey symbolizes the careful job search process. The ad ends with the HotJobs.com logo and website address, emphasizing the site's ability to help navigate the complexities of finding a job.  The overall tone is serious and focused on highlighting the service's value proposition.

title: Beauty Pagent
description: The ad is a comedic parody of a beauty pageant featuring WWF wrestlers.  The wrestlers, in glamorous attire, compete in typical pageant events, such as swimsuit and talent portions, with humorous twists reflecting their wrestling personas.  The humor comes from the juxtaposition of their tough personas with the elegance of the pageant setting and the unexpected events that unfold.

title: God
description: The 2000 Tabasco Super Bowl commercial depicts a man, seemingly God, creating the world.  He meticulously crafts various elements of nature, culminating in the creation of a bottle of Tabasco sauce, which he presents with a satisfied expression. The ad uses a dramatic, almost biblical tone, contrasting the grand scale of creation with the simple presentation of the condiment.  It subtly suggests Tabasco sauce is an essential element of existence, a humorous yet effective approach.

title: Sock Puppet
description: The Pets.com Super Bowl 2000 commercial features a sock puppet dog, who is the company mascot, dancing and singing a catchy jingle about the convenience and selection of Pets.com.  The sock puppet interacts with various backgrounds, seemingly highlighting the website's ease of use. The jingle is memorable and upbeat, focusing on the online pet supplies store's offerings.  The ad is primarily focused on the entertainment value of the sock puppet and the memorable tune, to attract viewers to the website.

title: Christopher Reeve Walks
description: The 2000 Nuveen Investments Super Bowl ad features Christopher Reeve, known for his role as Superman, in a wheelchair.  The ad focuses on Reeve's resilience and determination following his accident. It shows him working towards regaining mobility through physical therapy, ending with a powerful shot of him taking a few steps with assistance. The ad subtly connects this perseverance to the long-term investment strategies offered by Nuveen.

title: Cheetah
description: The Mountain Dew "Cheetah" Super Bowl ad from 2000 features a cheetah running incredibly fast through various landscapes, interspersed with quick cuts of people drinking Mountain Dew.  The cheetah's speed and energy are directly linked to the drink, suggesting it provides a similar boost.  The overall tone is energetic and action-packed, relying heavily on visual spectacle rather than a narrative.

title: Bohemian Rhapsody
description: The 2000 Mountain Dew Super Bowl commercial parodies Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody" music video.  It features a group of diverse young people engaging in various activities, such as skateboarding, mountain biking, and dancing, interspersed with scenes of them singing along to the song. The overall tone is energetic and rebellious, showcasing the brand's association with youth culture and an active lifestyle. The commercial concludes with a shot of a Dew bottle.

title: Cat Herding
description: The 2000 EDS Super Bowl commercial, titled "Cat Herding," uses a humorous analogy to illustrate the complexity of managing information technology.  The ad shows a cowboy attempting to herd cats, mirroring the challenges of integrating diverse systems.  The chaotic scenes of cats escaping and creating disorder visually represent the difficulties of managing IT infrastructure before EDS's solutions.  The ad concludes with a simple message highlighting EDS's ability to bring order to IT chaos.

title: Money Out Of The Wazoo
original_title: 2000 E*TRADE – Money Out Of The Wazoo
description: The 2000 E*TRADE Super Bowl commercial, "Money Out Of The Wazoo," features a cartoon-like depiction of a man overflowing with money.  He's initially overwhelmed by the abundance, then uses E*TRADE to manage his finances, ending with him relaxed and enjoying his wealth. The ad uses whimsical animation and humor to highlight the ease and convenience of online trading offered by E*TRADE.

title: Mike and Mike
description: The commercial features two Mikes, seemingly brothers, arguing playfully about which is better at using COMPUTER.COM.  One Mike boasts about finding a great deal on a computer, while the other counters with his own successful online shopping experience. The ad showcases the website's ease of use and wide selection of computers.  It ends with both Mikes agreeing that COMPUTER.COM is the best place to buy computers, emphasizing the convenience and user-friendly interface.

title: Rex
description: The Budweiser Super Bowl 2000 commercial, "Rex," features a Dalmatian puppy named Rex who is initially left behind by his owner.  Rex's determination to find his way back home is shown through a series of heartwarming scenes, including his encounter with other animals and his perseverance through various obstacles.  The commercial ends with a heartwarming reunion, emphasizing the loyalty and bond between the dog and his owner. The Budweiser logo appears subtly throughout.

title: Fred
description: The 2000 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial "Fred" features a Clydesdale foal named Fred struggling to keep up with the other horses in a Budweiser Clydesdale hitch.  The narrative follows Fred's journey as he perseveres, ultimately becoming a strong and capable member of the team.  The ad emphasizes themes of perseverance, determination, and the Budweiser brand's association with horses.

title: Show Us Your Can
description: The 2000 7UP Super Bowl commercial, "Show Us Your Can," features a diverse group of people engaging in various activities, all while holding or interacting with 7UP cans.  The ad emphasizes the refreshing and universally appealing nature of the soda. It uses quick cuts and energetic music to create a fast-paced, vibrant feel, showcasing the can as a central element in many different life scenarios.  The overall message promotes 7UP as a drink for everyone and any occasion.

title: Oz
description: The FedEx Super Bowl 2000 commercial, titled "Oz," features a whimsical, slightly surreal scenario.  A FedEx delivery person navigates a fantastical, Oz-like landscape, encountering various characters and challenges related to delivering a package.  The journey highlights the dedication and effort involved in ensuring timely and reliable package delivery, even in the face of the unexpected. The ad emphasizes FedEx's commitment to getting packages to their destination.

title: Bridal Boutique
description: The advertisement showcases a bridal boutique, highlighting the variety of wedding dresses available.  The video features several models displaying different gowns, emphasizing elegance and style. The setting is sophisticated, and the overall tone is aspirational, suggesting the boutique provides a high-end experience for brides-to-be.  Quick cuts between different dresses and models create a dynamic and engaging visual experience, highlighting the breadth of choices.

title: Nursery
description: The 2000 Oxygen.com Super Bowl commercial depicts a nursery setting where a baby monitor displays a seemingly mundane scene. However, the focus shifts to the adult's perspective through the monitor, revealing a provocative and unexpected adult setting. This juxtaposition creates a humorous contrast, highlighting Oxygen's edgy and unconventional content compared to traditional television.

title: Nerds
description: The 2000 Netpliance Super Bowl commercial, titled "Nerds," depicts a group of stereotypical nerds intensely focused on their computers.  The scene shifts to show them celebrating wildly as they achieve a technological breakthrough, likely related to Netpliance's internet appliances. The ad emphasizes the excitement and accomplishment associated with the technology, contrasting the geeky appearance of the users with their ultimate success.

title: Synchronized Swimmers
description: The VISA commercial features a synchronized swimming team performing a routine underwater.  The focus is on the precision and teamwork of the swimmers, mirroring the seamless and reliable nature of VISA transactions.  The ad concludes with the VISA logo and tagline, emphasizing the brand's global reach and consistent performance.  The overall tone is upbeat and positive, highlighting effortless efficiency. There's no spoken dialogue; the visuals drive the message.

title: We are the Champions
description: The 2000 AGILLION Super Bowl commercial, titled "We are the Champions," features a montage of diverse individuals engaged in various activities, set to the Queen song of the same name.  The visuals depict athletes, musicians, families, and everyday people, all seemingly empowered and successful.  The ad emphasizes a feeling of collective achievement and shared triumph, subtly suggesting AGILLION's role in enabling this success, although the product itself remains largely undefined throughout the commercial.

title: Feeling
description: The 2000 BMW X5 commercial emphasizes the vehicle's capability and driving experience.  The ad showcases the X5 navigating diverse terrains—from city streets to rugged off-road landscapes.  The visual style is sleek and modern, focusing on the car's performance and design. The overall message conveys a sense of freedom and adventure associated with owning the BMW X5.  The ad uses minimal dialogue, relying on visual storytelling and evocative music to create its impact.

title: She has a Cat
original_title: 2000 BUD LIGHT – She has a Cat
description: The 2000 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial features a man attempting to pick up a woman at a bar.  His attempts are repeatedly thwarted by humorous circumstances, mostly involving the woman's cat. The cat acts as a significant obstacle to his romantic pursuit, ultimately leading to a funny and slightly awkward conclusion where he ends up interacting with the cat more than the woman. The ad relies heavily on physical comedy and situational irony to create humor.

title: Hold the Door
description: The 2000 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial "Hold the Door" features a series of increasingly absurd scenarios where people desperately try to prevent a door from closing.  The humor stems from the escalating situations and the reactions of the characters.  The final scene shows a man using a Bud Light to wedge the door open, resolving the comical conflict. The ad emphasizes the lighthearted nature of the Bud Light brand.

title: Whaasup Game
description: The Budweiser "Whaasup" Super Bowl commercial features a series of phone calls between friends, each ending with the iconic question, "Whaasup?"  The conversations are punctuated by humorous reactions and situations.  The ad cleverly uses a repetitive format to showcase the camaraderie and shared experience of drinking Budweiser with friends, creating a memorable and funny scene. The commercial ends with a group of friends enjoying Budweiser together.

title: Monkey Dance
description: The ETRADE 2000 Super Bowl commercial, titled "Monkey Dance," features a group of monkeys dressed in business suits dancing energetically in a minimalist office setting.  The monkeys' synchronized movements and upbeat music create a humorous and memorable scene. The ad concludes with the ETRADE logo and tagline, subtly associating the brand with a playful, unconventional approach to investing.

title: Whaasup Pregame
description: The ad is a pre-game version of the iconic 'Wassup?' Budweiser commercial.  It shows a group of friends on a video call, playfully interacting and exchanging the signature greeting. The scene is set in a relaxed, casual setting, emphasizing camaraderie and friendship. The focus remains on the friendly exchange and the implied enjoyment of Budweiser amongst friends, with the beer itself minimally shown.

title: Hair
description: The 1999 Yahoo! Super Bowl commercial, titled "Hair," features a man obsessively focused on his hair.  He meticulously styles it throughout his day, using various products and techniques. The ad uses rapid cuts and quirky visuals, highlighting the man's dedication to his hairstyle and implicitly connecting it to the extensive information available on Yahoo!. The overall tone is humorous and slightly absurd, emphasizing Yahoo!'s position as a comprehensive online resource.

title: Cuba Gooding Jr.
description: The Pepsi One Super Bowl ad from 1999 features Cuba Gooding Jr.  He's in a futuristic, sleek setting, seemingly a party or club.  The ad emphasizes the 'one' aspect of Pepsi One, showing Gooding Jr. enjoying the drink.  Throughout the ad, there are quick cuts and stylistic choices, focusing on the modern and refreshing image of the product.  The ad is very short, relying on visual flair and Gooding Jr.'s star power to make an impact.

title: When I Grow Up
description: The 1999 Monster.com Super Bowl commercial, "When I Grow Up," features a montage of children expressing their future career aspirations.  These aspirations range from typical jobs like a doctor or astronaut to more unusual ones.  The commercial emphasizes the vast array of career possibilities and subtly positions Monster.com as a tool to help people find their ideal job.  The overall tone is upbeat and optimistic, using diverse children to represent a wide range of potential career paths.

title: Eat, Sleep, Drink Football
description: The 1999 Coca-Cola Super Bowl commercial, "Eat, Sleep, Drink Football," uses a montage style to depict various individuals' obsession with football.  Scenes include people engrossed in games, celebrating touchdowns, and even dreaming about football.  The ad emphasizes the pervasive nature of football's influence on everyday life, connecting it to simple activities like eating and sleeping.  Coca-Cola is subtly integrated into the scenes, appearing as a refreshing beverage alongside the passion for the sport.

title: Ali Landry
description: The 1999 Doritos Super Bowl commercial features Ali Landry, then relatively unknown.  The ad's core concept centers on a playful interaction between Landry and a man. She playfully teases him by dropping a Doritos chip. The man's increasingly desperate attempts to retrieve the chip from the floor culminate in a humorous, slightly awkward ending where he picks it up and eats it. The focus is on the deliciousness of Doritos implied by the man's actions.

title: Separated At Birth
description: The 1999 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "Separated at Birth," features a comedic split-screen comparison of two Clydesdale horses, one in a pristine Budweiser stable and the other struggling in a muddy, less-than-ideal environment.  The visual juxtaposition highlights the superior care and upbringing of the Budweiser Clydesdales, implicitly associating the brand with quality and attention to detail.  The ad concludes with the familiar Budweiser logo and tagline.

title: Lobster
description: A Budweiser commercial from 1999 featuring a lobster in a tank.  The lobster is shown in various scenarios, including being dressed in a tiny tuxedo and seemingly enjoying a Budweiser.  The ad uses humor and quirky visuals to associate the beer with a unique, memorable image. The overall tone is lighthearted and playful, aiming for comedic effect rather than a serious message. There's no clear narrative beyond the lobster's antics.

title: Got Canned
description: The 1999 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "Got Canned," features a group of frogs playing in a swamp.  A larger frog is trying to get the attention of a female frog.  He is continually interrupted by other frogs and eventually gets canned (fired) from his position by a larger, authoritative frog. The commercial ends with the tagline: "Budweiser.  The King of Beers."

title: Coach “Anti-Refreshment Syndicate”
description: The 1999 7UP Super Bowl commercial features a coach leading a team of quirky athletes through various unusual training exercises.  The athletes are comically inept, highlighting the absurdity of conventional sports training. The ad's humor stems from the unexpected and silly situations, culminating in a final scene with the team celebrating their unorthodox success. The overall message is subtly anti-establishment, suggesting 7UP is a refreshing alternative to the ordinary.

title: Willie
description: The 1999 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial "Willie" features a man named Willie who is incredibly unlucky.  A series of escalating mishaps befall him, from spilling his beer to a collapsing chair, all while his friends enjoy their Bud Lights.  The humor lies in the continuous string of misfortunes that plague Willie, contrasting with the carefree enjoyment of his companions. The ad concludes with Willie finally finding some good fortune, offering a lighthearted and relatable portrayal of everyday bad luck.

title: The Mummy
description: The advertisement is a trailer for the 1999 film "The Mummy."  It showcases scenes of intense action, suspenseful moments, and glimpses of the film's main characters.  The trailer uses dramatic music and quick cuts to build excitement and intrigue, highlighting the movie's adventure and horror elements.  It aims to generate interest in the film by showcasing its thrilling plot and visual spectacle.

title: Kenya Runner
description: The 1999 Just For Feet commercial depicts a barefoot Kenyan runner effortlessly outracing a pack of professional runners wearing high-tech shoes.  The ad emphasizes the natural running form and speed achieved without the aid of expensive footwear. The runner eventually stops and puts on a pair of Just For Feet shoes, implying enhanced performance but with a comical, almost surreal twist in pace.

title: Jon Lovitz
description: The 1999 Yellow Pages Super Bowl commercial features Jon Lovitz portraying a variety of characters who use the Yellow Pages to find various services.  The ad is fast-paced, showcasing quick cuts between Lovitz in different roles, each highlighting a different business listed in the directory.  The humor relies on Lovitz's comedic timing and the absurdity of the situations he's in, emphasizing the Yellow Pages' wide range of listings.

title: Start Something
description: The 1999 Oldsmobile Super Bowl commercial, "Start Something," showcases a diverse range of individuals pursuing their passions.  A young woman practices her ballet, a man works on his motorcycle, and a child plays with a toy car, all set against a vibrant backdrop of city life. The ad emphasizes the car's role in facilitating these pursuits, associating it with personal drive and ambition.  The overall tone is upbeat and aspirational, linking the Oldsmobile with the excitement of achieving personal goals.

title: World Chaos
description: The 1999 FirstUnion Financial Super Bowl commercial, titled "World Chaos," depicts a chaotic, surreal world where everyday events go hilariously wrong.  A man struggles with a stubborn door, a car spontaneously combusts, and a woman's hair inexplicably catches fire.  The absurdity culminates with a frustrated man throwing his hands up in exasperation.  The ad then transitions to a calmer scene, showcasing FirstUnion's services as a solution to the chaos, implying financial stability and reliability.

title: Paper or Plastic
description: The 1999 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, "Paper or Plastic," features a cashier asking a customer "Paper or Plastic?"  The customer, seemingly oblivious, engages in various absurd and humorous scenarios, including wrestling a bear, riding a horse, and skydiving, before finally returning to the checkout, still unsure of his choice.  The humor derives from the unexpected, unrelated actions interjected into the mundane grocery store setting, highlighting the lighthearted and carefree nature of Bud Light.

title: Fashion Show
description: The 1999 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show features a variety of models showcasing the brand's lingerie and clothing.  The show includes elaborate sets, musical performances, and various themed segments.  Models walk the runway in different styles of lingerie, showcasing the collection's diversity. The overall tone is glamorous and celebratory, highlighting the brand's aspirational image and the beauty of the models.

title: Louie Slapped Around
description: The 1999 Budweiser Super Bowl commercial, "Louie Slapped Around," features the Budweiser frogs.  A fly lands on Louie's head, causing him to repeatedly slap himself in a comical manner.  The other frogs watch and eventually join in the slapping. The ad ends with the Budweiser frogs singing their signature jingle. The humor focuses on the frogs' physical reactions and slapstick comedy.

title: Hal
description: The 1999 Apple "Hal" Super Bowl commercial features a young boy who uses an iMac to create a digital animation of a surreal, dreamlike world.  The animation is imaginative and vibrant, showcasing the iMac's capabilities.  The ad concludes with the Apple logo and tagline.  The focus is on the creative potential unlocked by the technology, rather than specific features.

title: Cartoons
description: The 1999 Mastercard Super Bowl commercial features a series of animated vignettes showcasing everyday moments made easier with a Mastercard.  The cartoons depict various scenarios, such as purchasing groceries, buying gas, and making a hotel reservation. The ad emphasizes the ease and convenience of using Mastercard for everyday transactions, employing a lighthearted and humorous tone throughout the series of quick scenes.

title: Honk Horn
description: The 1999 Volvo Trucks Super Bowl commercial, "Honk Horn," features a whimsical, cartoonish animation style.  A variety of people honk a Volvo truck's horn in various scenarios – a construction worker, a child, a couple, a farmer, etc.  The horn's sound triggers a chain reaction of joyful, exaggerated movements and events, culminating in a large, celebratory gathering. The ad emphasizes the sound and presumably, the overall quality of the Volvo truck.

title: AirCrisps
description: The 1999 Nabisco AirCrisps Super Bowl commercial features a whimsical, cartoon-like animation.  A group of diverse individuals are shown enjoying AirCrisps in various settings.  The animation style is lighthearted and playful, emphasizing the airy and light texture of the snack. The commercial focuses on the product's crispness and overall enjoyable eating experience, showcasing different people enjoying the snack in different situations.

title: Seinfeld
description: The 1999 American Express Super Bowl commercial features Jerry Seinfeld and his friends at Monk's diner.  They discuss everyday frustrations and mundane events, highlighting the relatable aspects of life.  The ad subtly uses the setting and dialogue to emphasize the value of the American Express card as a reliable tool for everyday transactions. The humor stems from the familiar Seinfeld dynamic and relatable situations, rather than grand gags or slapstick.

title: Montero Sport
description: The 1999 Mitsubishi Montero Sport commercial showcases the SUV's rugged capabilities.  The ad features various shots of the vehicle traversing diverse terrains, including off-road driving and city streets.  Quick cuts and dynamic camera angles emphasize the vehicle's agility and strength.  The emphasis is on the vehicle's performance and suitability for an active lifestyle, with little to no dialogue or narrative.

title: with Halle Berry
description: The 1999 MMS Crispy Super Bowl commercial features Halle Berry enjoying a bag of MMS Crispy candy.  The ad uses a split-screen showing Berry's glamorous lifestyle juxtaposed with everyday moments of people enjoying the candy. The overall message is that MMS Crispy is a delicious and enjoyable snack that fits into various lifestyles.  The focus is on the product and its taste, with minimal storyline or dramatic events.

title: Bathroom
description: The 1999 Visa Check Card commercial depicts a man in a bathroom, meticulously preparing for a date.  He uses his Visa card to buy various items, shown in quick cuts.  The commercial emphasizes the convenience and speed of using a Visa check card for everyday purchases, highlighting its practicality.  The humorous element comes from the man's exaggerated pre-date routine and his implied anxiety about his appearance.

title: Really Big Bag
description: The 1999 Cracker Jack Super Bowl commercial showcases an enormous bag of Cracker Jack appearing on a baseball field, dwarfing players and spectators.  A boy expresses his amazement at the sheer size. The ad emphasizes the fun and joy associated with the snack, focusing on the large size of the bag as a key selling point. It's a simple, lighthearted spot with a focus on the product's scale and association with baseball.

title: World Headquarters
description: The 1999 WWF Super Bowl ad, "World Headquarters," showcases various WWF wrestlers in a comedic and chaotic setting.  The wrestlers are shown interacting in a parody of a typical office environment, complete with office workers and mundane office tasks.  The humor derives from the juxtaposition of the wrestlers' aggressive personas with the everyday office setting, creating a series of slapstick moments and silly conflicts.  The ad concludes with a promotional message for the WWF.

title: PJs’ Promo
description: This 1999 Super Bowl commercial for FOX promotes its sitcom "PJs."  The ad features short clips showcasing the show's characters and humorous situations.  It uses quick cuts and energetic music to highlight the show's comedic style and diverse cast. The overall tone is lighthearted and aims to entice viewers to watch the series. The ad is primarily focused on showcasing comedic moments from the sitcom, rather than explicitly promoting any other product.

title: Zoo
description: The 1999 Hartford Insurance commercial, titled "Zoo," depicts a variety of animals behaving like humans in various office settings. A gorilla sits at a desk, a bear uses a computer, and a monkey makes phone calls.  The overall tone is humorous, highlighting the unexpected and slightly chaotic nature of daily life, suggesting that Hartford Insurance can handle life's unpredictable events.  The ad ends with the Hartford logo and tagline.

title: Cyberspace
description: The 1999 BUY.com Super Bowl commercial, titled "Cyberspace," depicts a futuristic, surreal journey through a digital landscape.  A young man navigates a vibrant, otherworldly environment filled with animated graphics and computer-generated imagery.  He encounters various bizarre and humorous situations, showcasing the vast selection and novelty offered by BUY.com. The ad emphasizes the website's expansive online catalog, positioning it as a portal to a limitless shopping experience in the burgeoning age of e-commerce.

title: Austin Powers
description: The 1999 Super Bowl commercial for Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery features a montage of clips from the film.  It showcases Mike Myers as Austin Powers, his comedic interactions with various characters, and glimpses of the film's action and spy-themed antics.  The ad relies heavily on the film's already established humor and quirky style to generate interest in the movie's release.  The fast-paced editing highlights key scenes and memorable moments, intending to entice viewers to see the full movie.

title: Stanley Cup
description: The 1999 FedEx Super Bowl commercial shows a FedEx delivery person meticulously navigating various obstacles to deliver a Stanley Cup to its destination.  The ad highlights the reliability and precision of FedEx delivery services, showcasing the driver's dedication and the company's ability to handle even time-sensitive, high-value packages. The focus is on the journey and the safe arrival of the prized trophy, emphasizing FedEx's commitment to efficient and successful delivery.

title: Sky Surfing with Goose
description: The 1998 Pepsi Super Bowl commercial features actor and comedian, Dan Aykroyd, as a sky surfer.  He's seen soaring through the air on a Pepsi-branded board, performing various stunts and tricks, with the tagline "Pepsi: The Choice of a New Generation."  The ad is fast-paced and action-packed, showcasing Aykroyd's comedic timing and the excitement of extreme sports.  It emphasizes the youthful energy associated with the Pepsi brand.

title: Mosquito
description: The 1998 Tabasco "Mosquito" Super Bowl commercial depicts a man enjoying a meal outdoors.  A mosquito lands on his food, and he reacts with exaggerated annoyance.  He then adds a generous amount of Tabasco sauce to his meal, seemingly using the heat to eliminate his pest problem. The ad uses humor and slapstick to showcase the product's use in everyday situations.

title: McKenzie Brothers from SCTV with Rick Moranis‎ and ‎Dave Thomas
original_title: 1998 MOLSON ICE – McKenzie Brothers from SCTV with Rick Moranis‎ and ‎Dave Thomas
description: The 1998 Molson Ice Super Bowl commercial features the McKenzie Brothers from SCTV, played by Dave Thomas and Rick Moranis.  They're in a hockey game, and their antics include fighting, questionable refereeing, and a bizarre ending involving a mysterious package and a celebratory beer.  The humor relies on the brothers' exaggerated personalities and slapstick actions within the context of a hockey game.

title: Jerry Seinfeld and Superman
original_title: 1998 AMERICAN EXPRESS – Jerry Seinfeld and Superman
description: Jerry Seinfeld is at a Superman-themed diner, encountering various Superman-related oddities.  He uses his American Express card for payment, highlighting its acceptance everywhere. Superman then dramatically appears, commending Seinfeld's card choice.  The ad emphasizes the card's widespread acceptance, even in fictional, fantastical settings. The humor relies on the juxtaposition of the mundane (paying a bill) with the extraordinary (Superman's presence).

title: Michael Richards Athletic Campaign
description: The 1998 Hilfiger Super Bowl ad features actor Michael Richards, known for his role as Kramer on Seinfeld.  The commercial opens with Richards in various athletic scenarios, including playing basketball, running track, and boxing. The scenes are interspersed with shots of Hilfiger clothing and a somewhat comedic tone.  Richards' comedic timing and unexpected athletic endeavors are the focus, highlighting the brand's association with a popular celebrity and suggesting a connection between Hilfiger clothing and athleticism.

title: Do you see any Bud Light?
original_title: 1998 BUD LIGHT – Do you see any Bud Light?
description: The 1998 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial features a man meticulously searching a bar for a Bud Light, encountering various humorous obstacles and distractions.  He eventually finds one, only to discover it's empty. The humor lies in the absurdity of his dedicated search and the ultimate anticlimactic reveal. The ad emphasizes the brand's presence and desirability in a playful way.

title: Out of Control
description: The 1998 Hormel Chili Super Bowl commercial, titled "Out of Control," depicts a chaotic scene at a chili cook-off.  A man enthusiastically eats chili, causing increasingly bizarre and escalating reactions –  objects flying, people dancing uncontrollably, and a general atmosphere of playful mayhem. The chili's deliciousness is implied to be the catalyst for this uncontrolled exuberance.  The ad ends with the Hormel Chili logo and tagline.

title: Gus
description: The 1998 Volvo Trucks Super Bowl commercial, "Gus," features a young boy and his dog, Gus, who is a trained dog and seemingly works for Volvo.  The ad focuses on the reliability and toughness of Volvo trucks through a series of shots showcasing Gus's abilities, including hauling a small wagon across varied terrains, navigating obstacles, and even acting as a 'helper' on the jobsite. The ad ends with a shot of the Volvo truck and the tagline, implying the truck's capabilities are akin to Gus's hard work and dependability.

title: Last Rice Krispies Treat
description: A young boy meticulously crafts a Rice Krispies Treat, carefully arranging marshmallows and using a special pan.  He shares it with his family, offering each person a piece. The final piece remains untouched, symbolizing the preciousness of the treat and the shared family moment. The ad ends with a close-up shot of the last remaining piece, showcasing the product and emphasizing the simple joy of Kellogg's Rice Krispies Treats.

title: Chicken Plays Pool
description: A Bud Light commercial from 1998 features a chicken playing pool with surprisingly skilled precision.  The chicken meticulously lines up shots, sinks balls, and even shows a bit of cocky swagger.  The ad uses comedic exaggeration to highlight the unexpected and lighthearted nature of the Bud Light brand.  The overall tone is playful and absurd, relying entirely on the visual gag of a chicken playing pool with human-like skill.

title: Mask of Zorro
description: The 1998 Super Bowl commercial for Sony Pictures' "The Mask of Zorro" showcases dramatic scenes from the film.  It features Antonio Banderas as Zorro, highlighting his swashbuckling sword fights, daring escapes, and romantic encounters.  The fast-paced editing emphasizes the action and adventure, culminating in a shot of the film's title card.  The ad relies heavily on visual storytelling to pique viewer interest.

title: Dick Clark
description: The 1998 M&M's Super Bowl commercial features Dick Clark, iconic American Bandstand host.  The ad uses a split-screen format. On one side, Clark introduces M&M's in a classic Bandstand style. On the other side, various scenarios show people enjoying M&M's candies in different settings. The commercial is light-hearted and emphasizes the candy's fun and enjoyable nature, with a focus on its appeal across various demographics.  The overall tone is upbeat and nostalgic, leveraging Clark's presence to connect with a wider audience.

title: Traded
description: The 1998 Royal Caribbean "Traded" Super Bowl ad depicts a bustling city scene where people seemingly trade their everyday lives – a briefcase for a cruise ship, a desk job for a beach – to escape to a Royal Caribbean cruise.  The ad emphasizes the freedom and escape offered by a cruise vacation, contrasting the ordinary with the extraordinary. It uses quick cuts and upbeat music to convey a sense of excitement and adventure.

title: Russian Nuclear Facility
description: The 1998 Network Associates Super Bowl ad depicts a tense scene at a Russian nuclear facility.  A technician struggles with a computer system, facing a potential meltdown.  Network Associates' security software is shown to swiftly resolve the critical situation, preventing disaster. The ad emphasizes the software's reliability and ability to handle high-stakes security threats in a dramatic and suspenseful manner, showcasing its power and efficacy.

title: Angela likes Bobby
description: The 1998 AT&T commercial depicts a young woman named Angela and her attempts to connect with Bobby.  The ad uses humorous scenarios where Angela repeatedly tries to reach Bobby via phone, showcasing AT&T's reliable service.  The situations are comedically exaggerated, ending with Angela successfully connecting and Bobby's surprised reaction. The ad focuses on the ease and dependability of AT&T's phone service.

title: Bug sings ‘Brown Sugar’
description: A Pepsi commercial from 1998 features a cartoon bug, anthropomorphized with a human-like face and clothing, performing a cover of The Rolling Stones' "Brown Sugar." The bug is shown singing and playing the song on a stage in front of a crowd of insects.  The ad is primarily focused on the humorous contrast between the insect character and the familiar rock song.  The Pepsi logo is prominently displayed throughout.

title: Wile E Coyote Vs. Road Runner Wide Track
original_title: 1998 PONTIAC GRAND PRIX – Wile E Coyote Vs. Road Runner Wide Track
description: The Super Bowl ad features Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner.  Wile E. Coyote uses various gadgets in his pursuit of the Road Runner, showcasing the Pontiac Grand Prix's handling and speed. The Road Runner consistently outsmarts Coyote, highlighting the car's superior performance.  The humor relies on the classic cartoon dynamic and ends with the Road Runner leaving Coyote in a cloud of dust, emphasizing the Grand Prix's power and agility.

title: Jeff Gordon
description: The 1998 Pepsi commercial features NASCAR driver Jeff Gordon racing a Pepsi-branded car.  He's shown driving at high speeds, performing impressive maneuvers, and ultimately winning the race.  The ad emphasizes speed, excitement, and the association of Pepsi with a winning attitude and thrilling moments.  Quick cuts and dynamic camera angles create a sense of urgency and energy throughout.

title: Evil Beavers
description: The 1998 Miller Lite Super Bowl commercial features two beavers, portrayed as mischievous villains, sabotaging a lumberjack's efforts.  The beavers use various tools and tactics to thwart the lumberjack's attempts to cut down trees, culminating in a chaotic scene where the beavers triumph.  The ad ends with the Miller Lite logo and tagline, emphasizing the comedic clash between the lumberjack and the surprisingly clever beavers. The humor lies in the unexpected intelligence and cunning displayed by the beavers.

title: Babe Ruth
description: The 1998 Lipton Brisk commercial features Babe Ruth, portrayed by an actor, in a modern-day setting.  He's shown enjoying a refreshing Brisk iced tea while engaging in various activities like playing video games and relaxing. The ad uses humor and a juxtaposition of the legendary baseball player with contemporary situations to create a lighthearted and memorable advertisement for the iced tea brand.

title: Zip Drive
description: The 1998 IOMEGA Zip Drive Super Bowl commercial showcases the convenience and speed of the Zip drive.  The ad features a variety of people in various scenarios using the Zip drive to quickly transfer large files, contrasting it with the slowness of older methods.  Scenes depict a businessman on a plane, a photographer, and people in an office environment.  The overall message emphasizes efficiency and ease of use.

title: Ali Landry
description: The 1998 Doritos Super Bowl commercial features Ali Landry, who is playfully interacting with a man at a party.  She subtly seduces him, leading to a moment of intense anticipation. The commercial's punchline involves a bag of Doritos, cleverly implying that the chips are the reason for the man's intense attraction to her. The scene is set in a lively party atmosphere, with music and other partygoers subtly in the background. The focus remains firmly on the interaction between Landry and the man.

title: Shopping
description: The 1998 Bud Light Super Bowl commercial, titled "Shopping," features a man and a woman shopping for groceries.  The man, frustrated with his shopping experience, repeatedly tries to grab a Bud Light from the shopping cart, only to be stopped by the woman.  The humorous conflict culminates with him finally enjoying a Bud Light outside after shopping. The commercial relies on simple, relatable scenarios of grocery shopping and couple dynamics to showcase the product.

title: Drew Carey Purple Connection
description: The 1998 Nokia commercial features Drew Carey interacting with various people in a purple-themed setting.  He uses a Nokia phone to connect with them, highlighting the phone's connectivity features. The humor derives from Carey's quirky personality and the unexpected situations he encounters.  The overall message promotes the Nokia phone's ability to bridge communication gaps, albeit in a comedic and surreal way. The commercial uses a purple color scheme consistently.
